n.12: The meaning of this verse is uncertain. Literally "And he made jambs, 60 cubits, and to the jamb of the court the gate all around, all around." Some take "he made" to mean "he measured". The Septuagint reads differently.
n.13: Hebrew *atumot*, perhaps "narrow", "latticed" or "with recessed frames" (1 Kings 6:4). Also in 41:16, 26.
n.14: Hebrew *elammot*, plural of *elam*, another form of *ulam*, "porch". Also in verses 21–36.
n.15: Carved palm trees, as on the walls of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6:29). Also in verses 22, 26, 31, 34 and 37.
n.16: The meaning of this verse is uncertain, and the Septuagint does not have it.
n.17: Hebrew *olah*, from the verb "go up": an animal burned whole on the altar (Leviticus 1). Also in verses 39 and 42.
n.18: Hebrew *chatta't*. Or "purification offering" (Leviticus 4).
n.19: Hebrew *asham*. Many scholars translate it "reparation offering" (Leviticus 5:14–6:7, 5:14–26 in the Hebrew).
n.20: Hebrew *gazit*: stone cut and dressed to shape.
n.21: Hebrew *shefattayim*, perhaps "double hooks" or "ledges". The meaning is uncertain.
n.22: The Septuagint reads "two rooms", and "the south gate" instead of "the east gate". The rooms in verses 45–46 are for priests.
n.23: Zadok was the priest whom Solomon made chief priest in place of Abiathar (1 Kings 2:35). In Ezekiel only his descendants may serve at the altar (43:19; 44:15–16).
n.24: The Septuagint adds "The width of the doorway was 14 cubits", and reads "the side walls of the doorway of the porch were 3 cubits on one side and 3 cubits on the other".
n.25: Literally "and by the steps by which they went up to it". The Septuagint reads "by ten steps".
n.26: Like the two bronze pillars that stood at the porch of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 7:15–22).

v: Then he brought me into the main hall[^1] and measured the jambs:[^2] 6 cubits[^3] wide on one side and 6 cubits wide on the other, the width of the tent.[^4]
וַיְבִיאֵ֖נִי אֶל־הַהֵיכָ֑ל וַיָּ֣מָד אֶת־הָאֵילִ֗ים שֵׁשׁ־אַמּ֨וֹת רֹ֧חַב מִפּ֛וֹ וְשֵׁשׁ־אַמּֽוֹת־רֹ֥חַב מִפּ֖וֹ רֹ֥חַב הָאֹֽהֶל׃
The entrance was 10 cubits wide, and the side walls of the entrance were 5 cubits on one side and 5 cubits on the other. He measured its length: 40 cubits; and its width: 20 cubits.
וְרֹ֣חַב הַפֶּתַח֮ עֶ֣שֶׂר אַמּוֹת֒ וְכִתְפ֣וֹת הַפֶּ֔תַח חָמֵ֤שׁ אַמּוֹת֙ מִפּ֔וֹ וְחָמֵ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת מִפּ֑וֹ וַיָּ֤מָד אָרְכּוֹ֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים אַמָּ֔ה וְרֹ֖חַב עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אַמָּֽה׃
Then he went inside and measured the jambs of the entrance: 2 cubits; the entrance: 6 cubits; and the width of the entrance: 7 cubits.[^5]
וּבָ֣א לִפְנִ֔ימָה וַיָּ֥מָד אֵֽיל־הַפֶּ֖תַח שְׁתַּ֣יִם אַמּ֑וֹת וְהַפֶּ֙תַח֙ שֵׁ֣שׁ אַמּ֔וֹת וְרֹ֥חַב הַפֶּ֖תַח שֶׁ֥בַע אַמּֽוֹת׃
He measured its length: 20 cubits; and its width: 20 cubits, at the far end of the main hall. He said to me, "This is the most holy place."[^6]
וַיָּ֨מָד אֶת־אָרְכּ֜וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אַמָּ֗ה וְרֹ֛חַב עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אַמָּ֖ה אֶל־פְּנֵ֣י הַֽהֵיכָ֑ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֖ה קֹ֥דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃
Then he measured the wall of the house:[^7] 6 cubits thick; and the width of the side rooms[^8] all around the house: 4 cubits.
וַיָּ֥מָד קִֽיר־הַבַּ֖יִת שֵׁ֣שׁ אַמּ֑וֹת וְרֹ֣חַב הַצֵּלָע֩ אַרְבַּ֨ע אַמּ֜וֹת סָבִ֧יב ׀ סָבִ֛יב לַבַּ֖יִת סָבִֽיב׃

The side rooms were one above another, thirty-three of them.[^9] There were ledges in the wall of the house all around for the side rooms, so that they would be supported, but they were not fastened into the wall of the house.[^10]

וְהַצְּלָעוֹת֩ צֵלָ֨ע אֶל־צֵלָ֜ע שָׁל֧וֹשׁ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים פְּעָמִ֗ים וּ֠בָאוֹת בַּקִּ֨יר אֲשֶׁר־לַבַּ֧יִת לַצְּלָע֛וֹת סָבִ֥יב ׀ סָבִ֖יב לִהְי֣וֹת אֲחוּזִ֑ים וְלֹֽא־יִהְי֥וּ אֲחוּזִ֖ים בְּקִ֥יר הַבָּֽיִת׃

The side rooms grew wider as they went around, story by story upward, for the structure around the house went up story by story all around the house. So the house was wider at the top, and one went up from the lowest story to the highest by way of the middle one.[^11]

וְֽרָחֲבָ֡ה וְֽנָסְבָה֩ לְמַ֨עְלָה לְמַ֜עְלָה לַצְּלָע֗וֹת כִּ֣י מֽוּסַב־הַ֠בַּיִת לְמַ֨עְלָה לְמַ֜עְלָה סָבִ֤יב ׀ סָבִיב֙ לַבַּ֔יִת עַל־כֵּ֥ן רֹֽחַב־לַבַּ֖יִת לְמָ֑עְלָה וְכֵ֧ן הַתַּחְתּוֹנָ֛ה יַעֲלֶ֥ה עַל־הָעֶלְיוֹנָ֖ה לַתִּיכוֹנָֽה׃
I saw that the house had a raised platform all around. The foundations of the side rooms were a full reed, 6 cubits to the edge.[^12]
וְרָאִ֧יתִי לַבַּ֛יִת גֹּ֖בַהּ סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֑יב *מיסדות **מוּסְד֤וֹת הַצְּלָעוֹת֙ מְל֣וֹ הַקָּנֶ֔ה שֵׁ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת אַצִּֽילָה׃
The thickness of the outer wall of the side rooms was 5 cubits. There was an open area[^13] beside the side structure of the house.
רֹ֣חַב הַקִּ֧יר אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־לַצֵּלָ֛ע אֶל־הַח֖וּץ חָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֑וֹת וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מֻנָּ֔ח בֵּ֥ית צְלָע֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר לַבָּֽיִת׃
Between the rooms there was a width of 20 cubits all around the house, on every side.[^14]
וּבֵ֨ין הַלְּשָׁכ֜וֹת רֹ֣חַב עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אַמָּ֛ה סָבִ֥יב לַבַּ֖יִת סָבִ֥יב ׀ סָבִֽיב׃
The doorways of the side rooms opened onto the open area, one doorway toward the north and one doorway toward the south. The width of the open area was 5 cubits all around.
וּפֶ֤תַח הַצֵּלָע֙ לַמֻּנָּ֔ח פֶּ֤תַח אֶחָד֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן וּפֶ֥תַח אֶחָ֖ד לַדָּר֑וֹם וְרֹ֙חַב֙ מְק֣וֹם הַמֻּנָּ֔ח חָמֵ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת סָבִ֥יב ׀ סָבִֽיב׃
The building that faced the separate yard[^15] on the west side[^16] was 70 cubits wide. The wall of the building was 5 cubits thick all around, and its length was 90 cubits.
וְהַבִּנְיָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ אֶל־פְּנֵ֨י הַגִּזְרָ֜ה פְּאַ֣ת דֶּֽרֶךְ־הַיָּ֗ם רֹ֚חַב שִׁבְעִ֣ים אַמָּ֔ה וְקִ֧יר הַבִּנְיָ֛ן חָֽמֵשׁ־אַמּ֥וֹת רֹ֖חַב סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֑יב וְאָרְכּ֖וֹ תִּשְׁעִ֥ים אַמָּֽה׃
Then he measured the house: 100 cubits long; and the separate yard and the building with its walls: 100 cubits long.
וּמָדַ֣ד אֶת־הַבַּ֔יִת אֹ֖רֶךְ מֵאָ֣ה אַמָּ֑ה וְהַגִּזְרָ֤ה וְהַבִּנְיָה֙ וְקִ֣ירוֹתֶ֔יהָ אֹ֖רֶךְ מֵאָ֥ה אַמָּֽה׃
The width of the front of the house and of the separate yard on the east was 100 cubits.
וְרֹחַב֩ פְּנֵ֨י הַבַּ֧יִת וְהַגִּזְרָ֛ה לַקָּדִ֖ים מֵאָ֥ה אַמָּֽה׃

He measured the length of the building facing the separate yard at the back of the house, with its galleries[^17] on either side: 100 cubits. The main hall, the inner room[^18] and the porches[^19] of the court,
וּמָדַ֣ד אֹֽרֶךְ־הַ֠בִּנְיָן אֶל־פְּנֵ֨י הַגִּזְרָ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עַל־אַחֲרֶ֧יהָ *ואתוקיהא **וְאַתִּיקֶ֛יהָא מִפּ֥וֹ וּמִפּ֖וֹ מֵאָ֣ה אַמָּ֑ה וְהַֽהֵיכָל֙ הַפְּנִימִ֔י וְאֻֽלַמֵּ֖י הֶחָצֵֽר׃

the thresholds, the narrow windows[^20] and the galleries all around the three of them, opposite the threshold, were paneled with wood all around, from the floor up to the windows; and the windows were covered.
הַסִּפִּ֡ים וְהַחַלּוֹנִ֣ים הָ֠אֲטֻמוֹת וְהָאַתִּיקִ֤ים ׀ סָבִיב֙ לִשְׁלָשְׁתָּ֔ם נֶ֧גֶד הַסַּ֛ף שְׂחִ֥יף עֵ֖ץ סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֑יב וְהָאָ֙רֶץ֙ עַד־הַֽחַלֹּנ֔וֹת וְהַֽחַלֹּנ֖וֹת מְכֻסּֽוֹת׃
Above the entrance, as far as the inner room and on the outside, and on all the walls all around, inside and outside, were measured panels.[^21]
עַל־מֵעַ֣ל הַפֶּ֡תַח וְעַד־הַבַּיִת֩ הַפְּנִימִ֨י וְלַח֜וּץ וְאֶל־כָּל־הַקִּ֨יר סָבִ֧יב ׀ סָבִ֛יב בַּפְּנִימִ֥י וּבַחִיצ֖וֹן מִדּֽוֹת׃
They were carved with cherubim[^22] and palm trees, with a palm tree between cherub and cherub. Each cherub had two faces:
וְעָשׂ֥וּי כְּרוּבִ֖ים וְתִֽמֹרִ֑ים וְתִֽמֹרָה֙ בֵּין־כְּר֣וּב לִכְר֔וּב וּשְׁנַ֥יִם פָּנִ֖ים לַכְּרֽוּב׃
a human face toward the palm tree on one side, and a lion's face toward the palm tree on the other side. They were carved on the whole temple all around.
וּפְנֵ֨י אָדָ֤ם אֶל־הַתִּֽמֹרָה֙ מִפּ֔וֹ וּפְנֵֽי־כְפִ֥יר אֶל־הַתִּֽמֹרָ֖ה מִפּ֑וֹ עָשׂ֥וּי אֶל־כָּל־הַבַּ֖יִת סָבִ֥יב ׀ סָבִֽיב׃
From the floor to above the entrance, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the main hall.[^23]
מֵהָאָ֙רֶץ֙ עַד־מֵעַ֣ל הַפֶּ֔תַח הַכְּרוּבִ֥ים וְהַתִּֽמֹרִ֖ים עֲשׂוּיִ֑ם וְקִ֖יר הַׄהֵׄיׄכָֽׄלׄ׃[4]
The doorposts of the main hall were square. In front of the holy place was something that looked like this:[^24]
הַֽהֵיכָ֖ל מְזוּזַ֣ת רְבֻעָ֑ה וּפְנֵ֣י הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ הַמַּרְאֶ֖ה כַּמַּרְאֶֽה׃
an altar of wood, 3 cubits high and 2 cubits long, with its corners. Its length[^25] and its walls were of wood. He said to me, "This is the table[^26] that is before the LORD."[^27]
הַמִּזְבֵּ֡חַ עֵ֣ץ שָׁלוֹשׁ֩ אַמּ֨וֹת גָּבֹ֜הַּ וְאָרְכּ֣וֹ שְׁתַּֽיִם־אַמּ֗וֹת וּמִקְצֹֽעוֹתָיו֙ ל֔וֹ וְאָרְכּ֥וֹ וְקִֽירֹתָ֖יו עֵ֑ץ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֚ה הַשֻּׁלְחָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
The main hall and the holy place each had a double door.
וּשְׁתַּ֧יִם דְּלָת֛וֹת לַֽהֵיכָ֖ל וְלַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
Each door had two leaves, two leaves that swung: two leaves for one door and two leaves for the other.
וּשְׁתַּ֥יִם דְּלָת֖וֹת לַדְּלָת֑וֹת שְׁ֚תַּיִם מוּסַבּ֣וֹת דְּלָת֔וֹת שְׁ֚תַּיִם לְדֶ֣לֶת אֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּ֥י דְלָת֖וֹת לָאַחֶֽרֶת׃
On the doors of the main hall were carved cherubim and palm trees like those carved on the walls. There was a canopy[^28] of wood on the front of the porch outside.
וַעֲשׂוּיָ֨ה אֲלֵיהֶ֜ן אֶל־דַּלְת֤וֹת הַֽהֵיכָל֙ כְּרוּבִ֣ים וְתִֽמֹרִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲשׂוּיִ֖ם לַקִּיר֑וֹת וְעָ֥ב עֵ֛ץ אֶל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאוּלָ֖ם מֵהַחֽוּץ׃
There were narrow windows and palm trees on either side, on the side walls of the porch, and on the side rooms of the house and on the canopies.
וְחַלּוֹנִ֨ים אֲטֻמ֤וֹת וְתִֽמֹרִים֙ מִפּ֣וֹ וּמִפּ֔וֹ אֶל־כִּתְפ֖וֹת הָֽאוּלָ֑ם וְצַלְע֥וֹת הַבַּ֖יִת וְהָעֻבִּֽים׃

n.1: Hebrew *heikhal*, "palace, temple": here the large main room of the temple, in front of the most holy place, as in Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6:3, 17). Traditionally "the temple" or "the nave".
n.2: Hebrew *elim*, probably the thick walls on either side of a passage (40:9). Also in verse 3.
n.3: The long cubit of 40:5, about 21 inches (53 cm). A reed (verse 8) was 6 such cubits, about 10½ feet (3.2 m).
n.4: Literally "the width of the tent". The meaning is uncertain.
n.5: The Septuagint reads "and the side walls of the entrance were 7 cubits on either side".
n.6: Literally "the holy of holies": the innermost room. Its measurements are those of the inner sanctuary of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6:20).
n.7: That is, the temple, as throughout chapters 40–48.
n.8: Hebrew *tsela*, "rib, side": rooms built against the outside of the temple walls, as in Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6:5–10).
n.9: Literally "side room to side room, three and thirty times". Many take this to mean three stories of thirty rooms each.
n.10: Compare 1 Kings 6:6. Literally "and they came into the wall that belonged to the house, for the side rooms all around, to be held, but they were not held in the wall of the house".
n.11: The meaning of this verse is uncertain. *The structure around* (Hebrew *musav*) may also mean a winding stair.
n.12: Hebrew *atsilah*, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps "to the edge" or "to the joint".
n.13: Hebrew *munnach*, "what is left": a free space or terrace. Also in verse 11. The meaning of verses 9–11 is uncertain.
n.14: Probably the rooms in the courts (40:17; 42:1–14). The open space between them and the temple was 20 cubits wide.
n.15: Hebrew *gizrah*, "cut-off area": an enclosed yard behind the temple, separated from the rest. Also in verses 13–15 and 42:1, 10, 13.
n.16: Literally "toward the sea", that is, the Mediterranean.
n.17: Hebrew *attiqim*, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps "galleries", "terraces" or "passages". Also in verse 16 and 42:3, 5.
n.18: Literally "and the inner main hall". The meaning is uncertain.
n.19: Hebrew *ulam*: an entrance hall or vestibule (40:7).
n.20: Hebrew *atumot*, perhaps "narrow" or "latticed" (40:16). Also in verse 26.
n.21: Hebrew *middot*, "measurements". The meaning of this verse is uncertain.
n.22: Hebrew *keruvim* (singular *keruv*, "cherub"): winged heavenly beings who guard holy places (Genesis 3:24; Exodus 25:18–22). Solomon's temple had carvings of cherubim and palm trees (1 Kings 6:29).
n.23: In the Hebrew text, dots are written over the word for "main hall", a scribal mark of doubt.
n.24: The meaning is uncertain. Literally "The main hall: a doorpost squared; and the front of the holy place: the appearance like the appearance." *The holy place* is probably the inner room (verse 4).
n.25: The Septuagint reads "2 cubits long and 2 cubits wide", and "its base" for "its length".
n.26: Perhaps the table for the bread of the Presence (Exodus 25:23–30), or an altar of incense (Exodus 30:1–10), which stood in front of the inner room.
n.27: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.28: Hebrew *av*, of uncertain meaning: perhaps a canopy, an overhang, or a threshold (1 Kings 7:6). Also in verse 26.

v: Then he brought me out into the outer court, by the way toward the north, and he brought me to the rooms opposite the separate yard[^1] and opposite the building on the north.
וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי אֶל־הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַצָּפ֑וֹן וָיְבִאֵ֣נִי אֶל־הַלִּשְׁכָּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נֶ֧גֶד הַגִּזְרָ֛ה וַאֲשֶֽׁר־נֶ֥גֶד הַבִּנְיָ֖ן אֶל־הַצָּפֽוֹן׃
Their length along the front, where the doorway faced north, was 100 cubits,[^2] and the width was 50 cubits.[^3]
אֶל־פְּנֵי־אֹ֙רֶךְ֙ אַמּ֣וֹת הַמֵּאָ֔ה פֶּ֖תַח הַצָּפ֑וֹן וְהָרֹ֖חַב חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אַמּֽוֹת׃
Opposite the 20 cubits that belonged to the inner court,[^4] and opposite the pavement that belonged to the outer court, was gallery[^5] facing gallery, in three stories.
נֶ֣גֶד הָֽעֶשְׂרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר֙ לֶחָצֵ֣ר הַפְּנִימִ֔י וְנֶ֣גֶד רִֽצְפָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֶחָצֵ֣ר הַחִֽיצוֹנָ֑ה אַתִּ֥יק אֶל־פְּנֵֽי־אַתִּ֖יק בַּשְּׁלִשִֽׁים׃
In front of the rooms was a passage 10 cubits wide, on the inner side, a way of 1 cubit,[^6] and their doorways were on the north.
וְלִפְנֵ֨י הַלְּשָׁכ֜וֹת מַהֲלַךְ֩ עֶ֨שֶׂר אַמּ֥וֹת רֹ֙חַב֙ אֶל־הַפְּנִימִ֔ית דֶּ֖רֶךְ אַמָּ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת וּפִתְחֵיהֶ֖ם לַצָּפֽוֹן׃
The upper rooms were narrower, for the galleries took more space from them than from the lower and the middle rooms of the building.
וְהַלְּשָׁכ֥וֹת הָעֶלְיוֹנֹ֖ת קְצֻר֑וֹת כִּֽי־יוֹכְל֨וּ אַתִּיקִ֜ים מֵהֵ֗נָה מֵֽהַתַּחְתֹּנ֛וֹת וּמֵהַתִּֽכֹנ֖וֹת בִּנְיָֽן׃
For they were in three stories and had no pillars like the pillars of the courts. So the upper rooms were set back from the ground more than the lower and the middle ones.
כִּ֤י מְשֻׁלָּשׁוֹת֙ הֵ֔נָּה וְאֵ֤ין לָהֶן֙ עַמּוּדִ֔ים כְּעַמּוּדֵ֖י הַחֲצֵר֑וֹת עַל־כֵּ֣ן נֶאֱצַ֗ל מֵהַתַּחְתּוֹנ֛וֹת וּמֵהַתִּֽיכֹנ֖וֹת מֵהָאָֽרֶץ׃
There was an outer wall parallel to the rooms, toward the outer court, in front of the rooms; it was 50 cubits long.
וְגָדֵ֤ר אֲשֶׁר־לַחוּץ֙ לְעֻמַּ֣ת הַלְּשָׁכ֔וֹת דֶּ֛רֶךְ הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַחִֽצוֹנָ֖ה אֶל־פְּנֵ֣י הַלְּשָׁכ֑וֹת אָרְכּ֖וֹ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אַמָּֽה׃
For the rooms on the side of the outer court were 50 cubits long, while those facing the main hall[^7] were 100 cubits.
כִּֽי־אֹ֣רֶךְ הַלְּשָׁכ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֶחָצֵ֥ר הַחִֽצוֹנָ֖ה חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֛ה עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַהֵיכָ֖ל מֵאָ֥ה אַמָּֽה׃
Below these rooms was the entryway from the east, as one enters them from the outer court.
*ומתחתה *לשכות **וּמִתַּ֖חַת **הַלְּשָׁכ֣וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה *המבוא **הַמֵּבִיא֙ מֵֽהַקָּדִ֔ים בְּבֹא֣וֹ לָהֵ֔נָּה מֵֽהֶחָצֵ֖ר הַחִצֹנָֽה׃
Along the width of the wall of the court toward the east,[^8] facing the separate yard and facing the building, were rooms,
בְּרֹ֣חַב ׀ גֶּ֣דֶר הֶחָצֵ֗ר דֶּ֧רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֛ים אֶל־פְּנֵ֧י הַגִּזְרָ֛ה וְאֶל־פְּנֵ֥י הַבִּנְיָ֖ן לְשָׁכֽוֹת׃
with a passage in front of them. They looked like the rooms on the north side; they had the same length and width, with all the same exits, arrangements and doorways.
וְדֶ֙רֶךְ֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם כְּמַרְאֵ֣ה הַלְּשָׁכ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁר֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן כְּאָרְכָּ֖ן כֵּ֣ן רָחְבָּ֑ן וְכֹל֙ מוֹצָ֣אֵיהֶ֔ן וּכְמִשְׁפְּטֵיהֶ֖ן וּכְפִתְחֵיהֶֽן׃
Like the doorways of the rooms on the south side was a doorway at the head of the passage, the passage in front of the matching wall,[^9] toward the east, as one enters them.
וּכְפִתְחֵ֣י הַלְּשָׁכ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁר֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֔וֹם פֶּ֖תַח בְּרֹ֣אשׁ דָּ֑רֶךְ דֶּ֗רֶךְ בִּפְנֵי֙ הַגְּדֶ֣רֶת הֲגִינָ֔ה דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֖ים בְּבוֹאָֽן׃

Then he said to me, "The north rooms and the south rooms facing the separate yard are the holy rooms, where the priests who come near to the LORD[^10] are to eat the most holy offerings.[^11] There they are to put the most holy offerings, the grain offering,[^12] the sin offering[^13] and the guilt offering,[^14] for the place is holy.

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י לִֽשְׁכ֨וֹת הַצָּפ֜וֹן לִֽשְׁכ֣וֹת הַדָּרוֹם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶל־פְּנֵ֣י הַגִּזְרָה֒ הֵ֣נָּה ׀ לִֽשְׁכ֣וֹת הַקֹּ֗דֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֹאכְלוּ־שָׁ֧ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־קְרוֹבִ֥ים לַֽיהוָ֖ה קָדְשֵׁ֣י הַקֳּדָשִׁ֑ים שָׁ֞ם יַנִּ֣יחוּ ׀ קָדְשֵׁ֣י הַקֳּדָשִׁ֗ים וְהַמִּנְחָה֙ וְהַחַטָּ֣את וְהָאָשָׁ֔ם כִּ֥י הַמָּק֖וֹם קָדֹֽשׁ׃

When the priests enter, they must not go out of the holy place into the outer court. They are to leave there the garments in which they minister, for these are holy, and they are to put on other garments before they go near the area for the people."

בְּבֹאָ֣ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים וְלֹֽא־יֵצְא֤וּ מֵהַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֣ר הַחִיצוֹנָ֔ה וְשָׁ֞ם יַנִּ֧יחוּ בִגְדֵיהֶ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־יְשָׁרְת֥וּ בָהֶ֖ן כִּֽי־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הֵ֑נָּה *ילבשו **וְלָבְשׁוּ֙ בְּגָדִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְקָרְב֖וּ אֶל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָעָֽם׃
When he had finished measuring the inner house,[^15] he brought me out by the gate that faced east and measured the area all around.
וְכִלָּ֗ה אֶת־מִדּוֹת֙ הַבַּ֣יִת הַפְּנִימִ֔י וְהוֹצִיאַ֙נִי֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַשַּׁ֔עַר אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּנָ֖יו דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֑ים וּמְדָד֖וֹ סָבִ֥יב ׀ סָבִֽיב׃
He measured the east side[^16] with the measuring reed: 500 reeds[^17] by the measuring reed, all around.
מָדַ֛ד ר֥וּחַ הַקָּדִ֖ים בִּקְנֵ֣ה הַמִּדָּ֑ה חֲמֵשׁ־*אמות **מֵא֥וֹת קָנִ֛ים בִּקְנֵ֥ה הַמִּדָּ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃
He measured the north side: 500 reeds by the measuring reed, all around.
מָדַ֖ד ר֣וּחַ הַצָּפ֑וֹן חֲמֵשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת קָנִ֛ים בִּקְנֵ֥ה הַמִּדָּ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃
He measured the south side: 500 reeds by the measuring reed.
אֵ֛ת ר֥וּחַ הַדָּר֖וֹם מָדָ֑ד חֲמֵשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת קָנִ֖ים בִּקְנֵ֥ה הַמִּדָּֽה׃
He turned to the west side and measured: 500 reeds by the measuring reed.
סָבַ֖ב אֶל־ר֣וּחַ הַיָּ֑ם מָדַ֛ד חֲמֵשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת קָנִ֖ים בִּקְנֵ֥ה הַמִּדָּֽה׃
He measured it on the four sides. It had a wall all around, 500 long and 500 wide, to separate the holy from the common.
לְאַרְבַּ֨ע רוּח֜וֹת מְדָד֗וֹ ח֤וֹמָה לוֹ֙ סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֔יב אֹ֚רֶךְ חֲמֵ֣שׁ מֵא֔וֹת וְרֹ֖חַב חֲמֵ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת לְהַבְדִּ֕יל בֵּ֥ין הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ לְחֹֽל׃

n.1: Hebrew *gizrah*, "cut-off area": the enclosed yard behind the temple (41:12). Also in verses 10 and 13.
n.2: The long cubit of 40:5, about 21 inches (53 cm). A reed (verse 16) was 6 such cubits, about 10½ feet (3.2 m).
n.3: The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain. Literally "To the face of the length of the 100 cubits, the doorway of the north, and the width 50 cubits."
n.4: The open space of 20 cubits around the temple (41:10).
n.5: Hebrew *attiq*, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps "gallery", "terrace" or "passage" (41:15). Also in verse 5.
n.6: The Septuagint and the Syriac read "100 cubits long".
n.7: Hebrew *heikhal*, the main room of the temple (41:1).
n.8: The Septuagint reads "toward the south", which fits verses 12–13.
n.9: Hebrew *haginah*, a word found only here, perhaps "matching". The meaning of this verse is uncertain.
n.10: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.11: Literally "the holy things of the holy things": the offerings of the highest degree of holiness, which only the priests could eat, and only in a holy place (Leviticus 6:9–11; 6:16–18 in most English Bibles).
n.12: Hebrew *minchah*, "gift, tribute": an offering of flour or grain (Leviticus 2).
n.13: Hebrew *chatta't*. Or "purification offering" (40:39).
n.14: Hebrew *asham*, perhaps "reparation offering" (40:39).
n.15: That is, the temple area inside the outer wall (40:5).
n.16: Hebrew *ruach*, "wind", here a direction or side. Also in verses 17–20.
n.17: The Hebrew text is written "5 cubits" but read "500". A side of 500 reeds would be 3,000 cubits, nearly a mile (1.6 km). Many think 500 cubits are meant here, as in 45:2: about 875 feet (265 m).

v: Then he led me to the gate, the gate that faces east.
וַיּוֹלִכֵ֖נִי אֶל־הַשָּׁ֑עַר שַׁ֕עַר אֲשֶׁ֥ר פֹּנֶ֖ה דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַקָּדִֽים׃
And there was the glory[^1] of the God of Israel, coming from the east. Its sound was like the sound of many waters, and the earth shone with his glory.
וְהִנֵּ֗ה כְּבוֹד֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּ֖א מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֑ים וְקוֹל֗וֹ כְּקוֹל֙ מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֔ים וְהָאָ֖רֶץ הֵאִ֥ירָה מִכְּבֹדֽוֹ׃
The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when I came to destroy the city,[^2] and the visions were like the vision I had seen by the river Chebar.[^3] And I fell on my face.
וּכְמַרְאֵ֨ה הַמַּרְאֶ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאִ֗יתִי כַּמַּרְאֶ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־רָאִ֙יתִי֙ בְּבֹאִי֙ לְשַׁחֵ֣ת אֶת־הָעִ֔יר וּמַרְא֕וֹת כַּמַּרְאֶ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי אֶל־נְהַר־כְּבָ֑ר וָאֶפֹּ֖ל אֶל־פָּנָֽי׃
The glory of the LORD[^4] came into the house[^5] by the gate that faces east.
וּכְב֥וֹד יְהוָ֖ה בָּ֣א אֶל־הַבָּ֑יִת דֶּ֣רֶךְ שַׁ֔עַר אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּנָ֖יו דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַקָּדִֽים׃
Then the Spirit[^6] lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and there the glory of the LORD filled the house.
וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי ר֔וּחַ וַתְּבִיאֵ֕נִי אֶל־הֶֽחָצֵ֖ר הַפְּנִימִ֑י וְהִנֵּ֛ה מָלֵ֥א כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה הַבָּֽיִת׃
I heard someone speaking to me from the house, while a man was standing beside me.
וָאֶשְׁמַ֛ע מִדַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֖י מֵהַבָּ֑יִת וְאִ֕ישׁ הָיָ֥ה עֹמֵ֖ד אֶצְלִֽי׃

He said to me, "Son of man,[^7] this is the place of my throne and the place of the soles of my feet, where I will live among the Israelites forever. The house of Israel will no longer defile my holy name, neither they nor their kings, by their prostitution[^8] and by the corpses[^9] of their kings at their death.[^10]

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י בֶּן־אָדָם֙ אֶת־מְק֣וֹם כִּסְאִ֗י וְאֶת־מְקוֹם֙ כַּפּ֣וֹת רַגְלַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֶשְׁכָּן־שָׁ֛ם בְּת֥וֹךְ בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְעוֹלָ֑ם וְלֹ֣א יְטַמְּא֣וּ ע֣וֹד בֵּֽית־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֞י הֵ֤מָּה וּמַלְכֵיהֶם֙ בִּזְנוּתָ֔ם וּבְפִגְרֵ֥י מַלְכֵיהֶ֖ם בָּמוֹתָֽם׃

When they set their threshold by my threshold and their doorpost beside my doorpost, with only a wall between me and them,[^11] they defiled my holy name by the detestable practices they committed. So I consumed them in my anger.
בְּתִתָּ֨ם סִפָּ֜ם אֶת־סִפִּ֗י וּמְזֽוּזָתָם֙ אֵ֣צֶל מְזוּזָתִ֔י וְהַקִּ֖יר בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וְטִמְּא֣וּ ׀ אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֗י בְּתֽוֹעֲבוֹתָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂ֔וּ וָאֲכַ֥ל אֹתָ֖ם בְּאַפִּֽי׃
Now let them put their prostitution and the corpses of their kings far away from me, and I will live among them forever.
עַתָּ֞ה יְרַחֲק֧וּ אֶת־זְנוּתָ֛ם וּפִגְרֵ֥י מַלְכֵיהֶ֖ם מִמֶּ֑נִּי וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם׃ ס
As for you, son of man, describe the house to the house of Israel, so that they will be ashamed of their guilt. Let them measure its plan.[^12]
אַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם הַגֵּ֤ד אֶת־בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־הַבַּ֔יִת וְיִכָּלְמ֖וּ מֵעֲוֺנֽוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וּמָדְד֖וּ אֶת־תָּכְנִֽית׃

If they are ashamed of all they have done, make known to them the design of the house, its arrangement, its exits and its entrances, all its forms and all its decrees, all its forms and all its laws.[^13] Write it down before their eyes, so that they may keep its whole design and all its decrees and carry them out.

וְאִֽם־נִכְלְמ֞וּ מִכֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשׂ֗וּ צוּרַ֣ת הַבַּ֡יִת וּתְכוּנָת֡וֹ וּמוֹצָאָ֡יו וּמוֹבָאָ֣יו וְֽכָל־צֽוּרֹתָ֡ו וְאֵ֣ת כָּל־חֻקֹּתָיו֩ וְכָל־*צורתי **צ֨וּרֹתָ֤יו וְכָל־*תורתו **תּוֹרֹתָיו֙ הוֹדַ֣ע אוֹתָ֔ם וּכְתֹ֖ב לְעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וְיִשְׁמְר֞וּ אֶת־כָּל־צוּרָת֛וֹ וְאֶת־כָּל־חֻקֹּתָ֖יו וְעָשׂ֥וּ אוֹתָֽם׃
This is the law of the house: on the top of the mountain, the whole area all around will be most holy. Yes, this is the law of the house."
זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֣ת הַבָּ֑יִת עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָ֠הָר כָּל־גְּבֻל֞וֹ סָבִ֤יב ׀ סָבִיב֙ קֹ֣דֶשׁ קָדָשִׁ֔ים הִנֵּה־זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֥ת הַבָּֽיִת׃

These are the measurements of the altar in cubits, the cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth:[^14] its base is 1 cubit deep and 1 cubit wide, with a rim of 1 span[^15] around its edge. And this is the height[^16] of the altar:
וְאֵ֨לֶּה מִדּ֤וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ בָּֽאַמּ֔וֹת אַמָּ֥ה אַמָּ֖ה וָטֹ֑פַח וְחֵ֨יק הָאַמָּ֜ה וְאַמָּה־רֹ֗חַב וּגְבוּלָ֨הּ אֶל־שְׂפָתָ֤הּ סָבִיב֙ זֶ֣רֶת הָאֶחָ֔ד וְזֶ֖ה גַּ֥ב הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
From the base on the ground to the lower ledge it is 2 cubits, and the width is 1 cubit; and from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge it is 4 cubits, and the width is 1 cubit.
וּמֵחֵ֨יק הָאָ֜רֶץ עַד־הָעֲזָרָ֤ה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה֙ שְׁתַּ֣יִם אַמּ֔וֹת וְרֹ֖חַב אַמָּ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת וּמֵהֳעֲזָרָ֨ה הַקְּטַנָּ֜ה עַד־הָעֲזָרָ֤ה הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ אַרְבַּ֣ע אַמּ֔וֹת וְרֹ֖חַב הָאַמָּֽה׃
The altar hearth[^17] is 4 cubits high, and from the hearth four horns[^18] project upward.
וְהַֽהַרְאֵ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע אַמּ֑וֹת וּמֵהָאֲרִאֵ֣יל וּלְמַ֔עְלָה הַקְּרָנ֖וֹת אַרְבַּֽע׃
The altar hearth is square, 12 cubits long and 12 wide, square on its four sides.
*והאראיל **וְהָאֲרִיאֵ֗ל שְׁתֵּ֤ים עֶשְׂרֵה֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ בִּשְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה רֹ֑חַב רָב֕וּעַ אֶ֖ל אַרְבַּ֥עַת רְבָעָֽיו׃
The ledge is square, 14 cubits long and 14 wide on its four sides, with a rim around it of ½ cubit, and its base is 1 cubit all around. Its steps face east.

וְהָעֲזָרָ֞ה אַרְבַּ֧ע עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אֹ֗רֶךְ בְּאַרְבַּ֤ע עֶשְׂרֵה֙ רֹ֔חַב אֶ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣עַת רְבָעֶ֑יהָ וְהַגְּבוּל֩ סָבִ֨יב אוֹתָ֜הּ חֲצִ֣י הָאַמָּ֗ה וְהַֽחֵיק־לָ֤הּ אַמָּה֙ סָבִ֔יב וּמַעֲלֹתֵ֖הוּ פְּנ֥וֹת קָדִֽים׃

Then he said to me, "Son of man, this is what the Lord GOD[^19] says: These are the decrees for the altar on the day it is made, for offering burnt offerings[^20] on it and for splashing blood against it.
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י בֶּן־אָדָם֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה אֵ֚לֶּה חֻקּ֣וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ בְּי֖וֹם הֵעָֽשׂוֹת֑וֹ לְהַעֲל֤וֹת עָלָיו֙ עוֹלָ֔ה וְלִזְרֹ֥ק עָלָ֖יו דָּֽם׃
You are to give a young bull[^21] as a sin offering[^22] to the Levitical priests who are descendants of Zadok,[^23] who come near to me to serve me, declares the Lord GOD.
וְנָתַתָּ֣ה אֶל־הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים הַלְוִיִּ֡ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֵם֩ מִזֶּ֨רַע צָד֜וֹק הַקְּרֹבִ֣ים אֵלַ֗י נְאֻ֛ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה לְשָֽׁרְתֵ֑נִי פַּ֥ר בֶּן־בָּקָ֖ר לְחַטָּֽאת׃

You are to take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge and on the rim all around. So you will purify it from sin[^24] and make atonement for it.[^25]
וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ מִדָּמ֗וֹ וְנָ֨תַתָּ֜ה עַל־אַרְבַּ֤ע קַרְנֹתָיו֙ וְאֶל־אַרְבַּע֙ פִּנּ֣וֹת הָעֲזָרָ֔ה וְאֶֽל־הַגְּב֖וּל סָבִ֑יב וְחִטֵּאתָ֥ אוֹת֖וֹ וְכִפַּרְתָּֽהוּ׃
You are to take the bull of the sin offering and burn it in the appointed place of the house, outside the sanctuary.
וְלָ֣קַחְתָּ֔ אֵ֖ת הַפָּ֣ר הַֽחַטָּ֑את וּשְׂרָפוֹ֙ בְּמִפְקַ֣ד הַבַּ֔יִת מִח֖וּץ לַמִּקְדָּֽשׁ׃
On the second day you are to offer a male goat without defect as a sin offering, and they are to purify the altar as they purified it with the bull.
וּבַיּוֹם֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּקְרִ֛יב שְׂעִיר־עִזִּ֥ים תָּמִ֖ים לְחַטָּ֑את וְחִטְּאוּ֙ אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵ֔חַ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר חִטְּא֖וּ בַּפָּֽר׃
When you have finished purifying it, you are to offer a young bull without defect and a ram from the flock without defect.
בְּכַלּוֹתְךָ֖ מֵֽחַטֵּ֑א תַּקְרִיב֙ פַּ֣ר בֶּן־בָּקָ֣ר תָּמִ֔ים וְאַ֥יִל מִן־הַצֹּ֖אן תָּמִֽים׃
You are to present them before the LORD, and the priests are to throw salt[^26] on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD.
וְהִקְרַבְתָּ֖ם לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְהִשְׁלִ֨יכוּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים עֲלֵיהֶם֙ מֶ֔לַח וְהֶעֱל֥וּ אוֹתָ֛ם עֹלָ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃
For seven days you are to provide a goat for a sin offering each day. A young bull and a ram from the flock, without defect, are also to be provided.
שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה שְׂעִיר־חַטָּ֖את לַיּ֑וֹם וּפַ֧ר בֶּן־בָּקָ֛ר וְאַ֥יִל מִן־הַצֹּ֖אן תְּמִימִ֥ים יַעֲשֽׂוּ׃
For seven days they are to make atonement for the altar and cleanse it, and so consecrate it.[^27]
שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֗ים יְכַפְּרוּ֙ אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְטִֽהֲר֖וּ אֹת֑וֹ וּמִלְא֖וּ *ידו **יָדָֽיו׃

When they have completed these days, from the eighth day on, the priests are to offer your burnt offerings and your fellowship offerings[^28] on the altar, and I will accept you, declares the Lord GOD."

וִֽיכַלּ֖וּ אֶת־הַיָּמִ֑ים ס וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֜י וָהָ֗לְאָה יַעֲשׂ֨וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ אֶת־עוֹלֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ וְאֶת־שַׁלְמֵיכֶ֔ם וְרָצִ֣אתִי אֶתְכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *kavod*, the visible splendor of God's presence (1:28). Ezekiel had seen it leave the temple by the east gate and stop on the mountain east of the city (10:18–19; 11:22–23).
n.2: That is, when Ezekiel was shown in his vision the destruction of the city (chapters 8–11).
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: That is, the temple, as throughout chapters 40–48.
n.6: Or "a spirit" or "a wind". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.7: Hebrew *ben adam*, "son of man": a human being, a mortal.
n.8: Hebrew *zenut*, "prostitution", an image for unfaithfulness to the LORD (6:9). Also in verse 9.
n.9: Or "the memorials". Hebrew *pigre*, usually "corpses". Also in verse 9.
n.10: The Hebrew is pointed *bamotam*, "their high places". The same consonants can be read *bemotam*, "at their death".
n.11: The royal palace was built beside the temple, so that only a wall separated them (1 Kings 7:1–12).
n.12: Hebrew *tokhnit*, "measurement, pattern" (28:12).
n.13: The Hebrew text is written "all its law" but read "all its laws".
n.14: The long cubit of 40:5, about 21 inches (53 cm).
n.15: Hebrew *zeret*, the span of the hand, ½ cubit: here about 10½ inches (27 cm).
n.16: Hebrew *gav*, "back", here perhaps the base or the height. The meaning is uncertain.
n.17: Hebrew *har'el* here and *ari'el* later in this verse and in verse 16: probably the hearth on top of the altar, where the fire burned. *Har'el* sounds like "mountain of God", and *ari'el* like "lion of God" (compare Isaiah 29:1).
n.18: The projections at the four corners of the altar (Exodus 27:2).
n.19: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles.
n.20: Hebrew *olah*: an animal burned whole on the altar (40:38; Leviticus 1).
n.21: Literally "a bull, a son of the herd". Also in verses 23 and 25.
n.22: Hebrew *chatta't*. Or "purification offering" (40:39). Also in verses 21, 22 and 25.
n.24: Hebrew *chitte'*, from the same root as *chatta't*, "sin offering". Also in verses 22 and 23.
n.25: Hebrew *kipper*, traditionally "make atonement". The word probably means "wipe clean, purge" (Leviticus 16:16–19). Also in verse 26.
n.27: Literally "fill its hands", an idiom for consecrating (Exodus 28:41). The Hebrew text is written "its hand" but read "its hands".

v: Then he brought me back by way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, the one facing east, and it was shut.
וַיָּ֣שֶׁב אֹתִ֗י דֶּ֣רֶךְ שַׁ֤עַר הַמִּקְדָּשׁ֙ הַֽחִיצ֔וֹן הַפֹּנֶ֖ה קָדִ֑ים וְה֖וּא סָגֽוּר׃
The LORD[^1] said to me, "This gate is to remain shut. It must not be opened, and no one may enter by it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered by it.[^2] So it is to remain shut.
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלַ֜י יְהוָ֗ה הַשַּׁ֣עַר הַזֶּה֩ סָג֨וּר יִהְיֶ֜ה לֹ֣א יִפָּתֵ֗חַ וְאִישׁ֙ לֹא־יָ֣בֹא ב֔וֹ כִּ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּ֣א ב֑וֹ וְהָיָ֖ה סָגֽוּר׃
Only the prince,[^3] because he is the prince, may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD. He is to enter by way of the porch of the gate and go out the same way."
אֶֽת־הַנָּשִׂ֗יא נָ֥שִׂיא ה֛וּא יֵֽשֶׁב־בּ֥וֹ לֶאֱכָול־לֶ֖חֶם לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה מִדֶּ֨רֶךְ אֻלָ֤ם הַשַּׁ֙עַר֙ יָב֔וֹא וּמִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ יֵצֵֽא׃
Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the house.[^4] I looked, and the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD, and I fell on my face.
וַיְבִיאֵ֜נִי דֶּֽרֶךְ־שַׁ֣עַר הַצָּפוֹן֮ אֶל־פְּנֵ֣י הַבַּיִת֒ וָאֵ֕רֶא וְהִנֵּ֛ה מָלֵ֥א כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וָאֶפֹּ֖ל אֶל־פָּנָֽי׃

The LORD said to me, "Son of man,[^5] pay attention, look with your eyes and listen with your ears to all that I tell you about all the decrees of the house of the LORD and all its laws.[^6] Pay attention to the entrance of the house and all the exits of the sanctuary.[^7]

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלַ֜י יְהֹוָ֗ה בֶּן־אָדָ֡ם שִׂ֣ים לִבְּךָ֩ וּרְאֵ֨ה בְעֵינֶ֜יךָ וּבְאָזְנֶ֣יךָ שְּׁמָ֗ע אֵ֣ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִי֙ מְדַבֵּ֣ר אֹתָ֔ךְ לְכָל־חֻקּ֥וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה וּלְכָל־*תורתו **תּֽוֹרֹתָ֑יו וְשַׂמְתָּ֤ לִבְּךָ֙ לִמְב֣וֹא הַבַּ֔יִת בְּכֹ֖ל מוֹצָאֵ֥י הַמִּקְדָּֽשׁ׃
Say to the rebellious,[^8] to the house of Israel, 'This is what the Lord GOD[^9] says: Enough of all your detestable practices,[^10] house of Israel!
וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֶל־מֶ֙רִי֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה רַב־לָכֶ֛ם מִֽכָּל־תּוֹעֲבֽ[m]וֹתֵיכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

You brought foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, into my sanctuary, to be in it and to profane my house, when you offered my food, the fat and the blood. They have broken my covenant,[^11] on top of all your detestable practices.

בַּהֲבִיאֲכֶ֣ם בְּנֵֽי־נֵכָ֗ר עַרְלֵי־לֵב֙ וְעַרְלֵ֣י בָשָׂ֔ר לִהְי֥וֹת בְּמִקְדָּשִׁ֖י לְחַלְּל֣וֹ אֶת־בֵּיתִ֑י בְּהַקְרִֽיבְכֶ֤ם אֶת־לַחְמִי֙ חֵ֣לֶב וָדָ֔ם וַיָּפֵ֙רוּ֙ אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֔י אֶ֖ל כָּל־תּוֹעֲבוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
You have not kept charge of my holy things yourselves; instead you have set them to keep my charge in my sanctuary for you.
וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת קָדָשָׁ֑י וַתְּשִׂימ֗וּן לְשֹׁמְרֵ֧י מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֛י בְּמִקְדָּשִׁ֖י לָכֶֽם׃
This is what the Lord GOD says: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, of all the foreigners who are among the Israelites, may enter my sanctuary.
כֹּה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ כָּל־בֶּן־נֵכָ֗ר עֶ֤רֶל לֵב֙ וְעֶ֣רֶל בָּשָׂ֔ר לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא אֶל־מִקְדָּשִׁ֑י לְכָל־בֶּן־נֵכָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֕ר בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
But the Levites who went far from me when Israel went astray, who went astray from me after their idols,[^12] will bear their guilt.
כִּ֣י אִם־הַלְוִיִּ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר רָֽחֲקוּ֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י בִּתְע֤וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תָּע֣וּ מֵֽעָלַ֔י אַחֲרֵ֖י גִּלּֽוּלֵיהֶ֑ם וְנָשְׂא֖וּ עֲוֺנָֽם׃

They will serve in my sanctuary, having charge of the gates of the house and serving the house. They will slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they will stand before the people to serve them.

וְהָי֤וּ בְמִקְדָּשִׁי֙ מְשָׁ֣רְתִ֔ים פְּקֻדּוֹת֙ אֶל־שַׁעֲרֵ֣י הַבַּ֔יִת וּֽמְשָׁרְתִ֖ים אֶת־הַבָּ֑יִת הֵ֠מָּה יִשְׁחֲט֨וּ אֶת־הָעֹלָ֤ה וְאֶת־הַזֶּ֙בַח֙ לָעָ֔ם וְהֵ֛מָּה יַעַמְד֥וּ לִפְנֵיהֶ֖ם לְשָֽׁרְתָֽם׃

Because they served them before their idols and became a stumbling block of guilt[^13] for the house of Israel, therefore I have raised my hand[^14] against them, declares the Lord GOD, swearing that they will bear their guilt.
יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְשָׁרְת֤וּ אוֹתָם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י גִלּֽוּלֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָי֥וּ לְבֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְמִכְשׁ֣וֹל עָוֺ֑ן עַל־כֵּן֩ נָשָׂ֨אתִי יָדִ֜י עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְנָשְׂא֖וּ עֲוֺנָֽם׃
They must not come near me to serve me as priests, or come near any of my holy things, the most holy things. They will bear their shame for the detestable practices they have committed.
וְלֹֽא־יִגְּשׁ֤וּ אֵלַי֙ לְכַהֵ֣ן לִ֔י וְלָגֶ֙שֶׁת֙ עַל־כָּל־קָ֣דָשַׁ֔י אֶל־קָדְשֵׁ֖י הַקְּדָשִׁ֑ים וְנָֽשְׂאוּ֙ כְּלִמָּתָ֔ם וְתוֹעֲבוֹתָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשֽׂוּ׃
Yet I will appoint them to keep charge of the house, for all its service and for all that is to be done in it.
וְנָתַתִּ֣י אוֹתָ֔ם שֹׁמְרֵ֖י מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת הַבָּ֑יִת לְכֹל֙ עֲבֹ֣דָת֔וֹ וּלְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה בּֽוֹ׃ פ

But the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok,[^15] who kept charge of my sanctuary when the Israelites went astray from me, they will come near to me to serve me. They will stand before me to offer me fat and blood, declares the Lord GOD.

וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים הַלְוִיִּ֜ם בְּנֵ֣י צָד֗וֹק אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁמְר֜וּ אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֤רֶת מִקְדָּשִׁי֙ בִּתְע֤וֹת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י הֵ֛מָּה יִקְרְב֥וּ אֵלַ֖י לְשָֽׁרְתֵ֑נִי וְעָמְד֣וּ לְפָנַ֗י לְהַקְרִ֥יב לִי֙ חֵ֣לֶב וָדָ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
They will enter my sanctuary, and they will come near to my table to serve me and keep my charge.
הֵ֜מָּה יָבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־מִקְדָּשִׁ֗י וְהֵ֛מָּה יִקְרְב֥וּ אֶל־שֻׁלְחָנִ֖י לְשָׁרְתֵ֑נִי וְשָׁמְר֖וּ אֶת־מִשְׁמַרְתִּֽי׃
When they enter the gates of the inner court, they are to wear linen garments. They must have nothing woolen on them while they serve in the gates of the inner court and inside the house.
וְהָיָ֗ה בְּבוֹאָם֙ אֶֽל־שַׁעֲרֵי֙ הֶחָצֵ֣ר הַפְּנִימִ֔ית בִּגְדֵ֥י פִשְׁתִּ֖ים יִלְבָּ֑שׁוּ וְלֹֽא־יַעֲלֶ֤ה עֲלֵיהֶם֙ צֶ֔מֶר בְּשָֽׁרְתָ֗ם בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֛י הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַפְּנִימִ֖ית וָבָֽיְתָה׃
They are to have linen turbans[^16] on their heads and linen undergarments around their waists. They must not wear anything that makes them sweat.
פַּאֲרֵ֤י פִשְׁתִּים֙ יִהְי֣וּ עַל־רֹאשָׁ֔ם וּמִכְנְסֵ֣י פִשְׁתִּ֔ים יִהְי֖וּ עַל־מָתְנֵיהֶ֑ם לֹ֥א יַחְגְּר֖וּ בַּיָּֽזַע׃

When they go out into the outer court, into the outer court to the people, they are to take off the garments in which they have been serving and leave them in the holy rooms, and put on other garments, so that they do not make the people holy by their garments.[^17]

וּ֠בְצֵאתָם אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֨ר הַחִיצוֹנָ֜ה אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֣ר הַחִיצוֹנָה֮ אֶל־הָעָם֒ יִפְשְׁט֣וּ אֶת־בִּגְדֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֙מָּה֙ מְשָׁרְתִ֣ם בָּ֔ם וְהִנִּ֥יחוּ אוֹתָ֖ם בְּלִֽשְׁכֹ֣ת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ וְלָֽבְשׁוּ֙ בְּגָדִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְלֹֽא־יְקַדְּשׁ֥וּ אֶת־הָעָ֖ם בְּבִגְדֵיהֶֽם׃
They must not shave their heads or let their hair grow long. They are to keep the hair of their heads trimmed.
וְרֹאשָׁם֙ לֹ֣א יְגַלֵּ֔חוּ וּפֶ֖רַע לֹ֣א יְשַׁלֵּ֑חוּ כָּס֥וֹם יִכְסְמ֖וּ אֶת־רָאשֵׁיהֶֽם׃
No priest may drink wine when he enters the inner court.
וְיַ֥יִן לֹֽא־יִשְׁתּ֖וּ כָּל־כֹּהֵ֑ן בְּבוֹאָ֖ם אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַפְּנִימִֽית׃
They must not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but only virgins of the descendants of the house of Israel, or a widow who is the widow of a priest.
וְאַלְמָנָה֙ וּגְרוּשָׁ֔ה לֹֽא־יִקְח֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם לְנָשִׁ֑ים כִּ֣י אִם־בְּתוּלֹ֗ת מִזֶּ֙רַע֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהָֽאַלְמָנָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה אַלְמָנָ֔ה מִכֹּהֵ֖ן יִקָּֽחוּ׃
They are to teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, and show them how to tell the unclean from the clean.
וְאֶת־עַמִּ֣י יוֹר֔וּ בֵּ֥ין קֹ֖דֶשׁ לְחֹ֑ל וּבֵין־טָמֵ֥א לְטָה֖וֹר יוֹדִעֻֽם׃
In a dispute they are to stand as judges, and they are to judge it by my rulings. They are to keep my laws and my decrees at all my appointed festivals, and they are to keep my Sabbaths holy.
וְעַל־רִ֗יב הֵ֚מָּה יַעַמְד֣וּ *לשפט **לְמִשְׁפָּ֔ט בְּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י *ושפטהו **יִשְׁפְּט֑וּהוּ וְאֶת־תּוֹרֹתַ֤י וְאֶת־חֻקֹּתַי֙ בְּכָל־מוֹעֲדַ֣י יִשְׁמֹ֔רוּ וְאֶת־שַׁבְּתוֹתַ֖י יְקַדֵּֽשׁוּ׃
A priest[^18] must not go near a dead person and so become unclean, except that for a father or mother, son or daughter, brother, or sister who has no husband, they may make themselves unclean.
וְאֶל־מֵ֣ת אָדָ֔ם לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא לְטָמְאָ֑ה כִּ֣י אִם־לְאָ֡ב וּ֠לְאֵם וּלְבֵ֨ן וּלְבַ֜ת לְאָ֗ח וּלְאָח֛וֹת אֲשֶֽׁר־לֹא־הָיְתָ֥ה לְאִ֖ישׁ יִטַּמָּֽאוּ׃
After he has been cleansed, seven days are to be counted for him.
וְאַחֲרֵ֖י טָֽהֳרָת֑וֹ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים יִסְפְּרוּ־לֽוֹ׃
On the day he enters the holy place, into the inner court, to serve in the holy place, he is to offer his sin offering,[^19] declares the Lord GOD.
וּבְיוֹם֩ בֹּא֨וֹ אֶל־הַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֤ר הַפְּנִימִית֙ לְשָׁרֵ֣ת בַּקֹּ֔דֶשׁ יַקְרִ֖יב חַטָּאת֑וֹ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
This is to be their inheritance: I am their inheritance. You are to give them no property in Israel; I am their property.
וְהָיְתָ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לְֽנַחֲלָ֔ה אֲנִ֖י נַֽחֲלָתָ֑ם וַאֲחֻזָּ֗ה לֹֽא־תִתְּנ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲנִ֖י אֲחֻזָּתָֽם׃
They are to eat the grain offering,[^20] the sin offering and the guilt offering,[^21] and everything devoted[^22] in Israel will be theirs.
הַמִּנְחָה֙ וְהַחַטָּ֣את וְהָאָשָׁ֔ם הֵ֖מָּה יֹֽאכְל֑וּם וְכָל־חֵ֥רֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לָהֶ֥ם יִהְיֶֽה׃

The best of all the firstfruits of every kind, and every contribution[^23] of every kind from all your contributions, will belong to the priests. You are to give the priest the first of your dough,[^24] so that a blessing may rest on your house.
וְרֵאשִׁית֩ כָּל־בִּכּ֨וּרֵי כֹ֜ל וְכָל־תְּר֣וּמַת כֹּ֗ל מִכֹּל֙ תְּרוּמ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים יִֽהְיֶ֑ה וְרֵאשִׁ֤ית עֲרִסֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ תִּתְּנ֣וּ לַכֹּהֵ֔ן לְהָנִ֥יחַ בְּרָכָ֖ה אֶל־בֵּיתֶֽךָ׃
The priests must not eat anything, bird or animal, that has died by itself or been torn by wild animals.
כָּל־נְבֵלָה֙ וּטְרֵפָ֔ה מִן־הָע֖וֹף וּמִן־הַבְּהֵמָ֑ה לֹ֥א יֹאכְל֖וּ הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃ פ

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: The glory of the LORD had entered by this gate (43:1–4).
n.3: Hebrew *nasi*, "leader, chief", Ezekiel's title for the ruler of Israel (34:24; 37:25). In chapters 44–48 he has a special place in the worship of the temple (45:7–17; 46:1–18).
n.4: That is, the temple, as throughout chapters 40–48.
n.5: Hebrew *ben adam*, "son of man": a human being, a mortal.
n.6: The Hebrew text is written "all its law" but read "all its laws".
n.7: That is, perhaps, to the rules for who may come in and go out (verses 6–9). Literally "Set your heart to the entrance of the house with all the exits of the sanctuary."
n.8: Literally "to rebellion".
n.9: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles. The message that begins here runs to 46:18.
n.10: Hebrew *to'evot*, things that are abhorrent, especially in worship. Also in verses 7 and 13.
n.11: The Septuagint, the Syriac and the Vulgate read "You have broken my covenant".
n.12: Hebrew *gillulim*, a contemptuous word for idols, perhaps related to the word for dung. Also in verse 12.
n.14: Literally "I have lifted my hand", the gesture of one who swears an oath (20:5).
n.15: See 40:46. The other Levites had served at the local shrines, the high places, before Josiah's reform (2 Kings 23:8–9).
n.16: Hebrew *pe'er*, a headdress, the word used for the priests' caps in Exodus 39:28.
n.17: That is, pass on holiness to the people by contact (Exodus 29:37; 30:29; Leviticus 6:20; 6:27 in most English Bibles).
n.18: Literally "He". The Hebrew moves between singular and plural in verses 25–27.
n.19: Hebrew *chatta't*. Or "purification offering" (40:39). Also in verse 29.
n.20: Hebrew *minchah*, "gift, tribute": an offering of flour or grain (Leviticus 2).
n.21: Hebrew *asham*, perhaps "reparation offering" (40:39).
n.22: Hebrew *cherem*: something irrevocably given over to the LORD (Leviticus 27:21, 28; Numbers 18:14).
n.23: Hebrew *terumah*: something set apart and given for a sacred purpose (Exodus 25:2; Numbers 18:8).
n.24: Hebrew *arisot*, probably coarse meal or dough (Numbers 15:20).

v: "'When you allot the land as an inheritance, you are to set apart a contribution[^1] for the LORD,[^2] a holy portion of the land, 25,000 long and 10,000 wide.[^3] It will be holy throughout its whole area all around.

וּבְהַפִּֽילְכֶ֨ם אֶת־הָאָ֜רֶץ בְּנַחֲלָ֗ה תָּרִימוּ֩ תְרוּמָ֨ה לַיהוָ֥ה ׀ קֹדֶשׁ֮ מִן־הָאָרֶץ֒ אֹ֗רֶךְ חֲמִשָּׁ֨ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֙לֶף֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ וְרֹ֖חַב עֲשָׂ֣רָה אָ֑לֶף קֹדֶשׁ־ה֥וּא בְכָל־גְּבוּלָ֖הּ סָבִֽיב׃
Of this, a square of 500 by 500 is to be for the sanctuary, with 50 cubits[^4] of open land around it.
יִהְיֶ֤ה מִזֶּה֙ אֶל־הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֛וֹת בַּחֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת מְרֻבָּ֣ע סָבִ֑יב וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֔ה מִגְרָ֥שׁ ל֖וֹ סָבִֽיב׃
From this measured area you are to measure off a section 25,000 long and 10,000 wide, and in it will be the sanctuary, the most holy place.
וּמִן־הַמִּדָּ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ תָּמ֔וֹד אֹ֗רֶךְ *חמש **חֲמִשָּׁ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף וְרֹ֖חַב עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת אֲלָפִ֑ים וּבֽוֹ־יִהְיֶ֥ה הַמִּקְדָּ֖שׁ קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָדָשִֽׁים׃
It is the holy portion of the land. It will be for the priests who serve in the sanctuary, who come near to serve the LORD. It will be a place for their houses and a holy area for the sanctuary.
קֹ֣דֶשׁ מִן־הָאָ֜רֶץ ה֗וּא לַכֹּ֨הֲנִ֜ים מְשָׁרְתֵ֤י הַמִּקְדָּשׁ֙ יִֽהְיֶ֔ה הַקְּרֵבִ֖ים לְשָׁרֵ֣ת אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וְהָיָ֨ה לָהֶ֤ם מָקוֹם֙ לְבָ֣תִּ֔ים וּמִקְדָּ֖שׁ לַמִּקְדָּֽשׁ׃
An area 25,000 long and 10,000 wide will belong to the Levites who serve the house,[^5] as their property, for twenty rooms.[^6]
וַחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֙לֶף֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ וַעֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִ֖ים רֹ֑חַב *יהיה **וְֽהָיָ֡ה לַלְוִיִּם֩ מְשָׁרְתֵ֨י הַבַּ֧יִת לָהֶ֛ם לַאֲחֻזָּ֖ה עֶשְׂרִ֥ים לְשָׁכֹֽת׃
Alongside the holy contribution you are to assign as the city's property an area 5,000 wide and 25,000 long. It will belong to the whole house of Israel.
וַאֲחֻזַּ֨ת הָעִ֜יר תִּתְּנ֗וּ חֲמֵ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ רֹ֔חַב וְאֹ֗רֶךְ חֲמִשָּׁ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף לְעֻמַּ֖ת תְּרוּמַ֣ת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ לְכָל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִהְיֶֽה׃

The prince[^7] is to have the land on both sides of the holy contribution and the city's property, alongside the holy contribution and the city's property, on the west side westward and on the east side eastward. Its length will correspond to one of the tribal portions, from the western border to the eastern border.[^8]

וְלַנָּשִׂ֡יא מִזֶּ֣ה וּמִזֶּה֩ לִתְרוּמַ֨ת הַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ וְלַאֲחֻזַּ֣ת הָעִ֗יר אֶל־פְּנֵ֤י תְרֽוּמַת־הַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ וְאֶל־פְּנֵי֙ אֲחֻזַּ֣ת הָעִ֔יר מִפְּאַת־יָ֣ם יָ֔מָּה וּמִפְּאַת־קֵ֖דְמָה קָדִ֑ימָה וְאֹ֗רֶךְ לְעֻמּוֹת֙ אַחַ֣ד הַחֲלָקִ֔ים מִגְּב֥וּל יָ֖ם אֶל־גְּב֥וּל קָדִֽימָה׃
This land will be his property in Israel. My princes will no longer oppress my people, but will give the rest of the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.
לָאָ֛רֶץ יִֽהְיֶה־לּ֥וֹ לַֽאֲחֻזָּ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹא־יוֹנ֨וּ ע֤וֹד נְשִׂיאַי֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י וְהָאָ֛רֶץ יִתְּנ֥וּ לְבֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְשִׁבְטֵיהֶֽם׃ ס
This is what the Lord GOD[^9] says: Enough, you princes of Israel! Put away violence and oppression, and do what is just and right. Stop evicting my people,[^10] declares the Lord GOD.
כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה רַב־לָכֶם֙ נְשִׂיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל חָמָ֤ס וָשֹׁד֙ הָסִ֔ירוּ וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה עֲשׂ֑וּ הָרִ֤ימוּ גְרֻשֹֽׁתֵיכֶם֙ מֵעַ֣ל עַמִּ֔י נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
You are to have honest scales, an honest ephah and an honest bath.[^11]
מֹֽאזְנֵי־צֶ֧דֶק וְאֵֽיפַת־צֶ֛דֶק וּבַת־צֶ֖דֶק יְהִ֥י לָכֶֽם׃
The ephah and the bath are to be the same size, the bath holding a tenth of a homer and the ephah a tenth of a homer. The homer[^12] is to be the standard measure for both.
הָאֵיפָ֣ה וְהַבַּ֗ת תֹּ֤כֶן אֶחָד֙ יִֽהְיֶ֔ה לָשֵׂ֕את מַעְשַׂ֥ר הַחֹ֖מֶר הַבָּ֑ת וַעֲשִׂירִ֤ת הַחֹ֙מֶר֙ הָֽאֵיפָ֔ה אֶל־הַחֹ֖מֶר יִהְיֶ֥ה מַתְכֻּנְתּֽוֹ׃
The shekel is to be 20 gerahs, and your mina is to be 20 shekels, 25 shekels and 15 shekels.[^13]
וְהַשֶּׁ֖קֶל עֶשְׂרִ֣ים גֵּרָ֑ה עֶשְׂרִ֨ים שְׁקָלִ֜ים חֲמִשָּׁ֧ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֣ים שְׁקָלִ֗ים עֲשָׂרָ֤ה וַחֲמִשָּׁה֙ שֶׁ֔קֶל הַמָּנֶ֖ה יִֽהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃
This is the contribution you are to present: a sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat, and a sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.
זֹ֥את הַתְּרוּמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר תָּרִ֑ימוּ שִׁשִּׁ֤ית הָֽאֵיפָה֙ מֵחֹ֣מֶר הַֽחִטִּ֔ים וְשִׁשִּׁיתֶם֙ הָֽאֵיפָ֔ה מֵחֹ֖מֶר הַשְּׂעֹרִֽים׃
The prescribed portion of oil, measured by the bath, is a tenth of a bath from each kor.[^14] A homer is 10 baths, for 10 baths are a homer.
וְחֹ֨ק הַשֶּׁ֜מֶן הַבַּ֣ת הַשֶּׁ֗מֶן מַעְשַׂ֤ר הַבַּת֙ מִן־הַכֹּ֔ר עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת הַבַּתִּ֖ים חֹ֑מֶר כִּֽי־עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת הַבַּתִּ֖ים חֹֽמֶר׃

And one sheep is to be given from every flock of two hundred, from the well-watered pastures of Israel, for grain offerings,[^15] burnt offerings[^16] and fellowship offerings,[^17] to make atonement[^18] for the people, declares the Lord GOD.
וְשֶׂה־אַחַ֨ת מִן־הַצֹּ֤אן מִן־הַמָּאתַ֙יִם֙ מִמַּשְׁקֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְמִנְחָ֖ה וּלְעוֹלָ֣ה וְלִשְׁלָמִ֑ים לְכַפֵּ֣ר עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
All the people of the land are to give this contribution to the prince in Israel.
כֹּ֚ל הָעָ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ יִהְי֖וּ אֶל־הַתְּרוּמָ֣ה הַזֹּ֑את לַנָּשִׂ֖יא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

It will be the prince's duty to provide the burnt offerings, the grain offerings and the drink offerings at the festivals, the new moons and the Sabbaths, at all the appointed festivals of the house of Israel. He is to provide the sin offering,[^19] the grain offering, the burnt offering and the fellowship offerings, to make atonement for the house of Israel.

וְעַֽל־הַנָּשִׂ֣יא יִהְיֶ֗ה הָעוֹל֣וֹת וְהַמִּנְחָה֮ וְהַנֵּסֶךְ֒ בַּחַגִּ֤ים וּבֶחֳדָשִׁים֙ וּבַשַּׁבָּת֔וֹת בְּכָֽל־מוֹעֲדֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הֽוּא־יַעֲשֶׂ֞ה אֶת־הַחַטָּ֣את וְאֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֗ה וְאֶת־הָֽעוֹלָה֙ וְאֶת־הַשְּׁלָמִ֔ים לְכַפֵּ֖ר בְּעַ֥ד בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ ס
This is what the Lord GOD says: In the first month, on the first day of the month, you are to take a young bull[^20] without defect and purify the sanctuary from sin.[^21]
כֹּה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ בָּֽרִאשׁוֹן֙ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ תִּקַּ֥ח פַּר־בֶּן־בָּקָ֖ר תָּמִ֑ים וְחִטֵּאתָ֖ אֶת־הַמִּקְדָּֽשׁ׃

The priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the house, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.
וְלָקַ֨ח הַכֹּהֵ֜ן מִדַּ֣ם הַחַטָּ֗את וְנָתַן֙ אֶל־מְזוּזַ֣ת הַבַּ֔יִת וְאֶל־אַרְבַּ֛ע פִּנּ֥וֹת הָעֲזָרָ֖ה לַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וְעַ֨ל־מְזוּזַ֔ת שַׁ֖עַר הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַפְּנִימִֽית׃
You are to do the same on the seventh day of the month[^22] for anyone who sins unintentionally or through ignorance. So you will make atonement for the house.
וְכֵ֤ן תַּֽעֲשֶׂה֙ בְּשִׁבְעָ֣ה בַחֹ֔דֶשׁ מֵאִ֥ישׁ שֹׁגֶ֖ה וּמִפֶּ֑תִי וְכִפַּרְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־הַבָּֽיִת׃
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you are to celebrate the Passover, a festival lasting a week,[^23] when bread made without yeast is to be eaten.
בָּ֠רִאשׁוֹן בְּאַרְבָּעָ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם הַפָּ֑סַח חָ֕ג שְׁבֻע֣וֹת יָמִ֔ים מַצּ֖וֹת יֵאָכֵֽל׃
On that day the prince is to provide, for himself and for all the people of the land, a bull as a sin offering.
וְעָשָׂ֤ה הַנָּשִׂיא֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא בַּעֲד֕וֹ וּבְעַ֖ד כָּל־עַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ פַּ֖ר חַטָּֽאת׃

During the seven days of the festival he is to provide as a burnt offering to the LORD seven bulls and seven rams without defect, each day for the seven days, and a male goat each day as a sin offering.
וְשִׁבְעַ֨ת יְמֵֽי־הֶחָ֜ג יַעֲשֶׂ֧ה עוֹלָ֣ה לַֽיהוָ֗ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת פָּ֠רִים וְשִׁבְעַ֨ת אֵילִ֤ים תְּמִימִם֙ לַיּ֔וֹם שִׁבְעַ֖ת הַיָּמִ֑ים וְחַטָּ֕את שְׂעִ֥יר עִזִּ֖ים לַיּֽוֹם׃
As a grain offering he is to provide an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, with a hin[^24] of oil for each ephah.
וּמִנְחָ֗ה אֵיפָ֥ה לַפָּ֛ר וְאֵיפָ֥ה לָאַ֖יִל יַֽעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְשֶׁ֖מֶן הִ֥ין לָאֵיפָֽה׃
In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the festival,[^25] he is to provide the same for seven days: the same sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings and oil.
בַּשְּׁבִיעִ֡י בַּחֲמִשָּׁה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר י֤וֹם לַחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ בֶּחָ֔ג יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה כָאֵ֖לֶּה שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים כַּֽחַטָּאת֙ כָּעֹלָ֔ה וְכַמִּנְחָ֖ה וְכַשָּֽׁמֶן׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *terumah*: something set apart and given for a sacred purpose (44:30). Also in verses 6, 7, 13 and 16, and in chapter 48.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: The unit is not given; probably the long cubit of 40:5, so that the area was about 8 miles by 3 miles (13 by 5.3 km). The Septuagint reads "20,000 wide", which fits verses 3–5 and 48:8–13. The area is described again in 48:8–22.
n.4: The long cubit of 40:5, about 21 inches (53 cm).
n.5: That is, the temple, as throughout chapters 40–48.
n.6: The Septuagint reads "for cities to live in".
n.7: Hebrew *nasi*, "leader, chief", the ruler of Israel (44:3). Also in verses 8, 9, 16, 17 and 22.
n.8: The land is divided into strips running from west to east, one for each tribe (chapter 48).
n.9: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles.
n.10: Literally "Lift your evictions from my people".
n.11: The ephah, a dry measure, and the bath, a liquid measure, were the same size (verse 11): probably about 22 liters, two-thirds of a bushel or about 6 gallons.
n.12: A homer was probably about 220 liters (6 bushels). The word means "donkey-load".
n.13: Together 60 shekels. A shekel was about ⅖ ounce (11.5 grams) and a gerah about 1/50 ounce (0.6 gram), so this mina was about 1½ pounds (690 grams).
n.14: A kor was the same size as a homer, about 220 liters.
n.15: Hebrew *minchah*, "gift, tribute": an offering of flour or grain (Leviticus 2). Also in verses 17, 24 and 25.
n.16: Hebrew *olah*: an animal burned whole on the altar (40:38; Leviticus 1).
n.17: Hebrew *shelamim*, traditionally "peace offerings" (Leviticus 3).
n.18: Hebrew *kipper*, traditionally "make atonement": "wipe clean, purge" (43:20). Also in verses 17 and 20.
n.19: Hebrew *chatta't*. Or "purification offering" (40:39). Also in verses 19, 22, 23 and 25.
n.20: Literally "a bull, a son of the herd".
n.21: Hebrew *chitte'*, from the same root as *chatta't*, "sin offering" (43:20).
n.22: The Septuagint reads "in the seventh month, on the first day of the month".
n.23: Literally "a festival of weeks of days".
n.24: A hin was about a gallon (4 liters).

v: "'This is what the Lord GOD[^1] says: The gate of the inner court that faces east is to be shut on the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it is to be opened, and on the day of the new moon it is to be opened.
כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ שַׁ֜עַר הֶחָצֵ֤ר הַפְּנִימִית֙ הַפֹּנֶ֣ה קָדִ֔ים יִהְיֶ֣ה סָג֔וּר שֵׁ֖שֶׁת יְמֵ֣י הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֑ה וּבְי֤וֹם הַשַּׁבָּת֙ יִפָּתֵ֔חַ וּבְי֥וֹם הַחֹ֖דֶשׁ יִפָּתֵֽחַ׃

The prince[^2] is to enter by way of the porch of the gate from outside and stand by the doorpost of the gate. The priests are to offer his burnt offering[^3] and his fellowship offerings,[^4] and he is to bow down at the threshold of the gate and then go out. But the gate is not to be shut until evening.

וּבָ֣א הַנָּשִׂ֡יא דֶּרֶךְ֩ אוּלָ֨ם הַשַּׁ֜עַר מִח֗וּץ וְעָמַד֙ עַל־מְזוּזַ֣ת הַשַּׁ֔עַר וְעָשׂ֣וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים אֶת־עֽוֹלָתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־שְׁלָמָ֔יו וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוָ֛ה עַל־מִפְתַּ֥ן הַשַּׁ֖עַר וְיָצָ֑א וְהַשַּׁ֥עַר לֹֽא־יִסָּגֵ֖ר עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃
The people of the land are to bow down at the entrance of that gate before the LORD on the Sabbaths and the new moons.
וְהִשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ עַם־הָאָ֗רֶץ פֶּ֚תַח הַשַּׁ֣עַר הַה֔וּא בַּשַּׁבָּת֖וֹת וּבֶחֳדָשִׁ֑ים לִפְנֵ֖י יְהוָֽה׃
The burnt offering that the prince presents to the LORD on the Sabbath day is to be six lambs without defect and a ram without defect.
וְהָ֣עֹלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־יַקְרִ֥ב הַנָּשִׂ֖יא לַֽיהוָ֑ה בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֗ת שִׁשָּׁ֧ה כְבָשִׂ֛ים תְּמִימִ֖ם וְאַ֥יִל תָּמִֽים׃
The grain offering[^5] is to be an ephah[^6] with the ram, and with the lambs as much as he wishes to give, and a hin of oil for each ephah.
וּמִנְחָה֙ אֵיפָ֣ה לָאַ֔יִל וְלַכְּבָשִׂ֥ים מִנְחָ֖ה מַתַּ֣ת יָד֑וֹ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן הִ֥ין לָאֵיפָֽה׃
On the day of the new moon he is to offer a young bull[^7] without defect, and six lambs and a ram, which are to be without defect.
וּבְי֣וֹם הַחֹ֔דֶשׁ פַּ֥ר בֶּן־בָּקָ֖ר תְּמִימִ֑ם וְשֵׁ֧שֶׁת כְּבָשִׂ֛ם וָאַ֖יִל תְּמִימִ֥ם יִהְיֽוּ׃
As a grain offering he is to provide an ephah with the bull and an ephah with the ram, and with the lambs as much as he can afford, and a hin of oil for each ephah.
וְאֵיפָ֨ה לַפָּ֜ר וְאֵיפָ֤ה לָאַ֙יִל֙ יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה מִנְחָ֔ה וְלַ֨כְּבָשִׂ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּשִּׂ֖יג יָד֑וֹ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן הִ֥ין לָאֵיפָֽה׃
When the prince enters, he is to come in by way of the porch of the gate and go out the same way.
וּבְב֖וֹא הַנָּשִׂ֑יא דֶּ֣רֶךְ אוּלָ֤ם הַשַּׁ֙עַר֙ יָב֔וֹא וּבְדַרְכּ֖וֹ יֵצֵֽא׃

When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to worship is to go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate is to go out by the north gate. No one is to go back through the gate by which he came in; each is to go out straight ahead.

וּבְב֨וֹא עַם־הָאָ֜רֶץ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֮ בַּמּֽוֹעֲדִים֒ הַבָּ֡א דֶּרֶךְ־שַׁ֨עַר צָפ֜וֹן לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֗ת יֵצֵא֙ דֶּרֶךְ־שַׁ֣עַר נֶ֔גֶב וְהַבָּא֙ דֶּרֶךְ־שַׁ֣עַר נֶ֔גֶב יֵצֵ֖א דֶּרֶךְ־שַׁ֣עַר צָפ֑וֹנָה לֹ֣א יָשׁ֗וּב דֶּ֤רֶךְ הַשַּׁ֙עַר֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֣א ב֔וֹ כִּ֥י נִכְח֖וֹ *יצאו **יֵצֵֽא׃
The prince is to be among them: when they come in, he is to come in, and when they go out, they are to go out.
וְֽהַנָּשִׂ֑יא בְּתוֹכָ֤ם בְּבוֹאָם֙ יָב֔וֹא וּבְצֵאתָ֖ם יֵצֵֽאוּ׃
At the festivals and the appointed times, the grain offering is to be an ephah with a bull and an ephah with a ram, and with the lambs as much as he wishes to give, and a hin of oil for each ephah.
וּבַחַגִּ֣ים וּבַמּוֹעֲדִ֗ים תִּהְיֶ֤ה הַמִּנְחָה֙ אֵיפָ֤ה לַפָּר֙ וְאֵיפָ֣ה לָאַ֔יִל וְלַכְּבָשִׂ֖ים מַתַּ֣ת יָד֑וֹ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן הִ֥ין לָאֵיפָֽה׃ ס

When the prince provides a freewill offering, a burnt offering or fellowship offerings as a freewill offering to the LORD, the gate that faces east is to be opened for him, and he is to offer his burnt offering and his fellowship offerings as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he is to go out, and after he has gone out the gate is to be shut.

וְכִֽי־יַעֲשֶׂה֩ הַנָּשִׂ֨יא נְדָבָ֜ה עוֹלָ֣ה אֽוֹ־שְׁלָמִים֮ נְדָבָ֣ה לַֽיהוָה֒ וּפָ֣תַֽח ל֗וֹ אֶת[c] הַשַּׁ֙עַר֙ הַפֹּנֶ֣ה קָדִ֔ים וְעָשָׂ֤ה אֶת־עֹֽלָתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־שְׁלָמָ֔יו כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת וְיָצָ֛א וְסָגַ֥ר אֶת־הַשַּׁ֖עַר אַחֲרֵ֥י צֵאתֽוֹ׃
You are to provide a year-old lamb without defect as a burnt offering to the LORD every day. Morning by morning you are to provide it.
וְכֶ֨בֶשׂ בֶּן־שְׁנָת֜וֹ תָּמִ֗ים תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה עוֹלָ֛ה לַיּ֖וֹם לַֽיהֹוָ֑ה בַּבֹּ֥קֶר בַּבֹּ֖קֶר תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתֽוֹ׃

With it, morning by morning, you are to provide a grain offering of a sixth of an ephah, with a third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour,[^8] a grain offering to the LORD. These are permanent decrees, to be kept continually.
וּמִנְחָה֩ תַעֲשֶׂ֨ה עָלָ֜יו בַּבֹּ֤קֶר בַּבֹּ֙קֶר֙ שִׁשִּׁ֣ית הָֽאֵיפָ֔ה וְשֶׁ֛מֶן שְׁלִישִׁ֥ית הַהִ֖ין לָרֹ֣ס אֶת־הַסֹּ֑לֶת מִנְחָה֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה חֻקּ֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ם תָּמִֽיד׃
So they are to provide the lamb, the grain offering and the oil morning by morning, as a regular burnt offering.
*ועשו **יַעֲשׂ֨וּ אֶת־הַכֶּ֧בֶשׂ וְאֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֛ה וְאֶת־הַשֶּׁ֖מֶן בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֑קֶר עוֹלַ֖ת תָּמִֽיד׃ פ
This is what the Lord GOD says: If the prince gives a gift to one of his sons, it is that son's inheritance and will belong to his sons. It is their property by inheritance.
כֹּה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה כִּֽי־יִתֵּ֨ן הַנָּשִׂ֤יא מַתָּנָה֙ לְאִ֣ישׁ מִבָּנָ֔יו נַחֲלָת֥וֹ הִ֖יא לְבָנָ֣יו תִּֽהְיֶ֑ה אֲחֻזָּתָ֥ם הִ֖יא בְּנַחֲלָֽה׃

But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it will belong to the servant until the year of liberty,[^9] and then it will return to the prince. His inheritance belongs to his sons alone; it is theirs.
וְכִֽי־יִתֵּ֨ן מַתָּנָ֜ה מִנַּחֲלָת֗וֹ לְאַחַד֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וְהָ֤יְתָה לּוֹ֙ עַד־שְׁנַ֣ת הַדְּר֔וֹר וְשָׁבַ֖ת לַנָּשִׂ֑יא אַ֚ךְ נַחֲלָת֔וֹ בָּנָ֖יו לָהֶ֥ם תִּהְיֶֽה׃

The prince must not take any of the people's inheritance, driving them off their property. He is to give his sons their inheritance from his own property, so that none of my people will be driven from his property.'"
וְלֹא־יִקַּ֨ח הַנָּשִׂ֜יא מִנַּחֲלַ֣ת הָעָ֗ם לְהֽוֹנֹתָם֙ מֵאֲחֻזָּתָ֔ם מֵאֲחֻזָּת֖וֹ יַנְחִ֣ל אֶת־בָּנָ֑יו לְמַ֙עַן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־יָפֻ֣צוּ עַמִּ֔י אִ֖ישׁ מֵאֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃
Then he brought me through the entrance at the side of the gate to the holy rooms for the priests, which faced north. There I saw a place at the far end,[^10] on the west side.
וַיְבִיאֵ֣נִי בַמָּבוֹא֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־כֶּ֣תֶף הַשַּׁעַר֒ אֶל־הַלִּשְׁכ֤וֹת הַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ אֶל־הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים הַפֹּנ֖וֹת צָפ֑וֹנָה וְהִנֵּה־שָׁ֣ם מָק֔וֹם *בירכתם **בַּיַּרְכָתַ֖יִם יָֽמָּה׃ ס

He said to me, "This is the place where the priests are to boil the guilt offering[^11] and the sin offering,[^12] and where they are to bake the grain offering, so that they do not bring them out into the outer court and make the people holy."[^13]

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֣ה הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יְבַשְּׁלוּ־שָׁם֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים אֶת־הָאָשָׁ֖ם וְאֶת־הַחַטָּ֑את אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֹאפוּ֙ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֔ה לְבִלְתִּ֥י הוֹצִ֛יא אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַחִֽיצוֹנָ֖ה לְקַדֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־הָעָֽם׃
Then he brought me out into the outer court and led me around to the four corners of the court, and in each corner of the court there was a court.
וַיּוֹצִיאֵ֗נִי אֶל־הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצֹנָ֔ה וַיַּ֣עֲבִירֵ֔נִי אֶל־אַרְבַּ֖עַת מִקְצוֹעֵ֣י הֶחָצֵ֑ר וְהִנֵּ֤ה חָצֵר֙ בְּמִקְצֹ֣עַ הֶחָצֵ֔ר חָצֵ֖ר בְּמִקְצֹ֥עַ הֶחָצֵֽר׃
In the four corners of the court were enclosed courts,[^14] 40 long and 30 wide.[^15] The four corner courts had the same measurements.[^16]
בְּאַרְבַּ֜עַת מִקְצֹע֤וֹת הֶֽחָצֵר֙ חֲצֵר֣וֹת קְטֻר֔וֹת אַרְבָּעִ֣ים אֹ֔רֶךְ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים רֹ֑חַב מִדָּ֣ה אַחַ֔ת לְאַרְבַּעְתָּ֖ם מְׄהֻׄקְׄצָׄעֽׄוֹׄתׄ׃[4]
Around each of the four of them was a row of stonework, and hearths for cooking were built under the rows all around.
וְט֨וּר סָבִ֥יב בָּהֶ֛ם סָבִ֖יב לְאַרְבַּעְתָּ֑ם וּמְבַשְּׁל֣וֹת עָשׂ֔וּי מִתַּ֥חַת הַטִּיר֖וֹת סָבִֽיב׃
He said to me, "These are the kitchens where those who serve the house[^17] will boil the sacrifices of the people."
וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י אֵ֚לֶּה בֵּ֣ית הַֽמְבַשְּׁלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר יְבַשְּׁלוּ־שָׁ֛ם מְשָׁרְתֵ֥י הַבַּ֖יִת אֶת־זֶ֥בַח הָעָֽם׃

n.1: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles. *The LORD* is God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. The message begun in 44:6 continues to verse 18.
n.2: Hebrew *nasi*, "leader, chief", the ruler of Israel (44:3).
n.3: Hebrew *olah*: an animal burned whole on the altar (40:38; Leviticus 1).
n.4: Hebrew *shelamim*, traditionally "peace offerings" (Leviticus 3). Also in verse 12.
n.5: Hebrew *minchah*, "gift, tribute": an offering of flour or grain (Leviticus 2).
n.6: An ephah was probably about 22 liters (two-thirds of a bushel), and a hin about a gallon (4 liters).
n.7: Literally "a bull, a son of the herd".
n.8: Hebrew *solet*, finely ground flour (Leviticus 2:1).
n.9: The year of Jubilee, every fiftieth year, when land returned to the families that owned it (Leviticus 25:10–13).
n.10: The Hebrew text is written "at their far end" but read "at the far end".
n.11: Hebrew *asham*, perhaps "reparation offering" (40:39).
n.12: Hebrew *chatta't*. Or "purification offering" (40:39).
n.13: That is, pass on holiness to the people by contact (44:19).
n.14: Hebrew *qeturot*, a word of uncertain meaning: perhaps "enclosed" or "small".
n.15: The unit is not given; probably the long cubit of 40:5, so that each court was about 70 by 52 feet (21 by 16 m).
n.16: In the Hebrew text, dots are written over the word for "corner", a scribal mark of doubt.
n.17: That is, the temple, as throughout chapters 40–48.

v: Then he brought me back to the entrance of the house,[^1] and there was water flowing out from under the threshold of the house toward the east, for the house faced east. The water was flowing down from under the south side[^2] of the house, south of the altar.

וַיְשִׁבֵנִי֮ אֶל־פֶּ֣תַח הַבַּיִת֒ וְהִנֵּה־מַ֣יִם יֹצְאִ֗ים מִתַּ֨חַת מִפְתַּ֤ן הַבַּ֙יִת֙ קָדִ֔ימָה כִּֽי־פְנֵ֥י הַבַּ֖יִת קָדִ֑ים וְהַמַּ֣יִם יֹרְדִ֗ים מִתַּ֜חַת מִכֶּ֤תֶף הַבַּ֙יִת֙ הַיְמָנִ֔ית מִנֶּ֖גֶב לַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
He brought me out by way of the north gate and led me around on the outside to the outer gate that faces east, and there the water was trickling out from the south side.
וַיּוֹצִאֵנִי֮ דֶּֽרֶךְ־שַׁ֣עַר צָפוֹנָה֒ וַיְסִבֵּ֙נִי֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ ח֔וּץ אֶל־שַׁ֣עַר הַח֔וּץ דֶּ֖רֶךְ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה קָדִ֑ים וְהִנֵּה־מַ֣יִם מְפַכִּ֔ים מִן־הַכָּתֵ֖ף הַיְמָנִֽית׃
As the man went out toward the east with a measuring line in his hand, he measured 1,000 cubits[^3] and led me through the water, and it was ankle-deep.
בְּצֵאת־הָאִ֥ישׁ קָדִ֖ים וְקָ֣ו בְּיָד֑וֹ וַיָּ֤מָד אֶ֙לֶף֙ בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה וַיַעֲבִרֵ֥נִי בַמַּ֖יִם מֵ֥י אָפְסָֽיִם׃
He measured another 1,000 and led me through the water, and it was knee-deep. He measured another 1,000 and led me through, and it was waist-deep.
וַיָּ֣מָד אֶ֔לֶף וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי בַמַּ֖יִם מַ֣יִם בִּרְכָּ֑יִם וַיָּ֣מָד אֶ֔לֶף וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֖נִי מֵ֥י מָתְנָֽיִם׃
He measured another 1,000, and it was a river that I could not cross, for the water had risen. It was deep enough to swim in, a river that could not be crossed.
וַיָּ֣מָד אֶ֔לֶף נַ֕חַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־אוּכַ֖ל לַעֲבֹ֑ר כִּֽי־גָא֤וּ הַמַּ֙יִם֙ מֵ֣י שָׂ֔חוּ נַ֖חַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יֵעָבֵֽר׃
He said to me, "Son of man,[^4] have you seen this?" Then he led me back along the bank of the river.
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלַ֖י הֲרָאִ֣יתָ בֶן־אָדָ֑ם וַיּוֹלִכֵ֥נִי וַיְשִׁבֵ֖נִי שְׂפַ֥ת הַנָּֽחַל׃
When I came back, there on the bank of the river were very many trees on both sides.
בְּשׁוּבֵ֕נִי וְהִנֵּה֙ אֶל־שְׂפַ֣ת הַנַּ֔חַל עֵ֖ץ רַ֣ב מְאֹ֑ד מִזֶּ֖ה וּמִזֶּֽה׃
He said to me, "This water flows out toward the eastern region and goes down into the Arabah,[^5] and it enters the sea. When it flows into the sea,[^6] the water of the sea will become fresh.[^7]
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י הַמַּ֤יִם הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ יוֹצְאִ֗ים אֶל־הַגְּלִילָה֙ הַקַּדְמוֹנָ֔ה וְיָרְד֖וּ עַל־הָֽעֲרָבָ֑ה וּבָ֣אוּ הַיָּ֔מָּה אֶל־הַיָּ֥מָּה הַמּֽוּצָאִ֖ים *ונרפאו **וְנִרְפּ֥וּ הַמָּֽיִם׃

Wherever the river[^8] goes, every living creature that swarms will live. There will be very many fish, because this water goes there and makes the water of the sea fresh; so everything will live where the river goes.

וְהָיָ֣ה כָל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֣ה ׀ אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־יִשְׁרֹ֡ץ אֶ֣ל כָּל־אֲשֶׁר֩ יָב֨וֹא שָׁ֤ם נַחֲלַ֙יִם֙ יִֽחְיֶ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה הַדָּגָ֖ה רַבָּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד כִּי֩ בָ֨אוּ שָׁ֜מָּה הַמַּ֣יִם הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְיֵרָֽפְאוּ֙ וָחָ֔י כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־יָ֥בוֹא שָׁ֖מָּה הַנָּֽחַל׃
Fishermen will stand beside it from En-gedi to En-eglaim;[^9] it will be a place for spreading nets. Its fish will be of many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea,[^10] very many.
וְהָיָה֩ *יעמדו **עָמְד֨וּ עָלָ֜יו דַּוָּגִ֗ים מֵעֵ֥ין גֶּ֙דִי֙ וְעַד־עֵ֣ין עֶגְלַ֔יִם מִשְׁט֥וֹחַ לַֽחֲרָמִ֖ים יִהְי֑וּ לְמִינָה֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה דְגָתָ֔ם כִּדְגַ֛ת הַיָּ֥ם הַגָּד֖וֹל רַבָּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃
But its swamps[^11] and marshes will not become fresh; they will be left for salt.
*בצאתו **בִּצֹּאתָ֧יו וּגְבָאָ֛יו וְלֹ֥א יֵרָפְא֖וּ לְמֶ֥לַח נִתָּֽנוּ׃

On both banks of the river every kind of tree for food will grow. Their leaves will not wither, and their fruit will not fail. They will bear fresh fruit every month, because their water flows from the sanctuary. Their fruit will be for food and their leaves for healing."[^12]

וְעַל־הַנַּ֣חַל יַעֲלֶ֣ה עַל־שְׂפָת֣וֹ מִזֶּ֣ה ׀ וּמִזֶּ֣ה ׀ כָּל־עֵֽץ־מַ֠אֲכָל לֹא־יִבּ֨וֹל עָלֵ֜הוּ וְלֹֽא־יִתֹּ֣ם פִּרְי֗וֹ לָֽחֳדָשָׁיו֙ יְבַכֵּ֔ר כִּ֣י מֵימָ֔יו מִן־הַמִּקְדָּ֖שׁ הֵ֣מָּה יֽוֹצְאִ֑ים *והיו **וְהָיָ֤ה פִרְיוֹ֙ לְמַֽאֲכָ֔ל וְעָלֵ֖הוּ לִתְרוּפָֽה׃ ס
"This is what the Lord GOD[^13] says: These are the boundaries by which you are to divide the land as an inheritance among the twelve tribes of Israel, with two portions for Joseph.[^14]
כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה גֵּ֤ה גְבוּל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּתְנַחֲל֣וּ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ לִשְׁנֵ֥י עָשָׂ֖ר שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יוֹסֵ֖ף חֲבָלִֽים׃
You are to divide it equally among you,[^15] the land I raised my hand[^16] to give to your ancestors. This land will fall to you as an inheritance.
וּנְחַלְתֶּ֤ם אוֹתָהּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ כְּאָחִ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָשָׂ֙אתִי֙ אֶת־יָדִ֔י לְתִתָּ֖הּ לַאֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם וְנָ֨פְלָ֜ה הָאָ֧רֶץ הַזֹּ֛את לָכֶ֖ם בְּנַחֲלָֽה׃
This is to be the boundary of the land: On the north side, from the Great Sea by the way of Hethlon, as one goes to Zedad,[^17]
וְזֶ֖ה גְּב֣וּל הָאָ֑רֶץ לִפְאַ֨ת צָפ֜וֹנָה מִן־הַיָּ֧ם הַגָּד֛וֹל הַדֶּ֥רֶךְ חֶתְלֹ֖ן לְב֥וֹא צְדָֽדָה׃
Hamath, Berothah and Sibraim, which lies between the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath, as far as Hazer-hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.[^18]
חֲמָ֤ת ׀ בֵּר֙וֹתָה֙ סִבְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁר֙ בֵּין־גְּב֣וּל דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וּבֵ֖ין גְּב֣וּל חֲמָ֑ת חָצֵר֙ הַתִּיכ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֶל־גְּב֥וּל חַוְרָֽן׃
So the boundary will run from the sea to Hazar-enan, at the border of Damascus, with the border of Hamath to the north. This is the north side.[^19]
וְהָיָ֨ה גְב֜וּל מִן־הַיָּ֗ם חֲצַ֤ר עֵינוֹן֙ גְּב֣וּל דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וְצָפ֥וֹן ׀ צָפ֖וֹנָה וּגְב֣וּל חֲמָ֑ת וְאֵ֖ת פְּאַ֥ת צָפֽוֹן׃

On the east side, the boundary will run between Hauran and Damascus, and along the Jordan between Gilead and the land of Israel. You are to measure from the northern boundary to the eastern sea.[^20] This is the east side.
וּפְאַ֣ת קָדִ֡ים מִבֵּ֣ין חַוְרָ֣ן וּמִבֵּין־דַּמֶּשֶׂק֩ וּמִבֵּ֨ין הַגִּלְעָ֜ד וּמִבֵּ֨ין אֶ֤רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן מִגְּב֛וּל עַל־הַיָּ֥ם הַקַּדְמוֹנִ֖י תָּמֹ֑דּוּ וְאֵ֖ת פְּאַ֥ת קָדִֽימָה׃
On the south side, toward the Negev, it will run from Tamar[^21] to the waters of Meribath-kadesh,[^22] and along the Wadi[^23] to the Great Sea. This is the south side, toward the Negev.
וּפְאַת֙ נֶ֣גֶב תֵּימָ֔נָה מִתָּמָ֗ר עַד־מֵי֙ מְרִיב֣וֹת קָדֵ֔שׁ נַחֲלָ֖ה אֶל־הַיָּ֣ם הַגָּד֑וֹל וְאֵ֥ת פְּאַת־תֵּימָ֖נָה נֶֽגְבָּה׃
On the west side, the Great Sea will be the boundary, as far as a point opposite Lebo-hamath.[^24] This is the west side.
וּפְאַת־יָם֙ הַיָּ֣ם הַגָּד֔וֹל מִגְּב֕וּל עַד־נֹ֖כַח לְב֣וֹא חֲמָ֑ת זֹ֖את פְּאַת־יָֽם׃
You are to divide this land among yourselves according to the tribes of Israel.
וְחִלַּקְתֶּ֞ם אֶת־הָאָ֧רֶץ הַזֹּ֛את לָכֶ֖ם לְשִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

You are to allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the foreigners who live among you and have had children among you. They are to be to you like native-born Israelites; with you they are to be allotted an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.

וְהָיָ֗ה תַּפִּ֣לוּ אוֹתָהּ֮ בְּנַחֲלָה֒ לָכֶ֗ם וּלְהַגֵּרִים֙ הַגָּרִ֣ים בְּתוֹכְכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הוֹלִ֥דוּ בָנִ֖ים בְּתֽוֹכְכֶ֑ם וְהָי֣וּ לָכֶ֗ם כְּאֶזְרָח֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִתְּכֶם֙ יִפְּל֣וּ בְנַחֲלָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
In whatever tribe the foreigner lives, there you are to give him his inheritance, declares the Lord GOD.
וְהָיָ֣ה בַשֵּׁ֔בֶט אֲשֶׁר־גָּ֥ר הַגֵּ֖ר אִתּ֑וֹ שָׁ֚ם תִּתְּנ֣וּ נַחֲלָת֔וֹ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ ס

n.1: That is, the temple, as throughout chapters 40–48.
n.2: Literally "the right side". Directions were given facing east, so the right side is the south. Also in verse 2.
n.3: The long cubit of 40:5, about 21 inches (53 cm), so 1,000 cubits was about a third of a mile (530 m).
n.4: Hebrew *ben adam*, "son of man": a human being, a mortal.
n.5: The deep rift valley of the Jordan and the Dead Sea.
n.6: Literally "into the sea, the ones brought out". The meaning is uncertain. *The sea* is the Dead Sea, whose water is too salty for fish to live in it.
n.7: Literally "will be healed". Also in verses 9 and 11.
n.8: Hebrew *nachalayim*, "two rivers", a dual form. The meaning is uncertain (compare Zechariah 14:8, where living waters flow both east and west).
n.9: En-gedi was an oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea. The site of En-eglaim is not known.
n.10: That is, the Mediterranean. Also in verses 15, 19 and 20.
n.11: The Hebrew text is written "when it goes out" but read "its swamps".
n.12: Compare Revelation 22:1–2.
n.13: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles. *The LORD* is God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. These words of the LORD run to the end of the book (48:35).
n.14: Literally "Joseph, portions". The descendants of Joseph's two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, each formed a tribe (Genesis 48:5; Joshua 14:4), so that there were twelve tribal portions without Levi (48:1–7, 23–29).
n.15: Literally "each man like his brother".
n.16: Literally "I lifted my hand", the gesture of one who swears an oath (20:5).
n.17: Literally "the way of Hethlon, to come to Zedad". Compare 48:1, "the way of Hethlon to Lebo-hamath", and Numbers 34:7–9.
n.18: These places, on the northern frontier in Syria, are mostly not known. *Hazer-hatticon* means "the middle Hazer"; *Hauran* is the region east of the Sea of Galilee.
n.19: Literally "and the north side". Also in verses 18 and 19; verse 20 has "This is the west side".
n.20: The Septuagint and the Syriac read "to the eastern sea, as far as Tamar" (compare verse 19). The eastern sea is the Dead Sea.
n.21: A place south of the Dead Sea (1 Kings 9:18).
n.22: Meribah at Kadesh, in the wilderness south of Canaan (Numbers 20:13; 27:14).
n.23: The Wadi of Egypt, probably the Wadi el-Arish (Numbers 34:5).
n.24: Or "the entrance to Hamath": the northern frontier of Israel (Numbers 34:8).

v: "These are the names of the tribes: At the northern end, beside the way of Hethlon to Lebo-hamath, as far as Hazar-enan, at the border of Damascus, with Hamath to the north beside it, and extending from the east side to the west side,[^1] Dan will have one portion.

וְאֵ֖לֶּה שְׁמ֣וֹת הַשְּׁבָטִ֑ים מִקְצֵ֣ה צָפ֡וֹנָה אֶל־יַ֣ד דֶּֽרֶךְ־חֶתְלֹ֣ן ׀ לְֽבוֹא־חֲמָ֡ת חֲצַ֣ר עֵינָן֩ גְּב֨וּל דַּמֶּ֤שֶׂק צָפ֙וֹנָה֙ אֶל־יַ֣ד חֲמָ֔ת וְהָיוּ־ל֧וֹ פְאַת־קָדִ֛ים הַיָּ֖ם דָּ֥ן אֶחָֽד׃
Next to the territory of Dan, from the east side to the west side, Asher will have one portion.
וְעַ֣ל ׀ גְּב֣וּל דָּ֗ן מִפְּאַ֥ת קָדִ֛ים עַד־פְּאַת־יָ֖מָּה אָשֵׁ֥ר אֶחָֽד׃
Next to the territory of Asher, from the east side to the west side, Naphtali will have one portion.
וְעַ֣ל ׀ גְּב֣וּל אָשֵׁ֗ר מִפְּאַ֥ת קָדִ֛ימָה וְעַד־פְּאַת־יָ֖מָּה נַפְתָּלִ֥י אֶחָֽד׃
Next to the territory of Naphtali, from the east side to the west side, Manasseh will have one portion.
וְעַ֣ל ׀ גְּב֣וּל נַפְתָּלִ֗י מִפְּאַ֥ת קָדִ֛מָה עַד־פְּאַת־יָ֖מָּה מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃
Next to the territory of Manasseh, from the east side to the west side, Ephraim will have one portion.
וְעַ֣ל ׀ גְּב֣וּל מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה מִפְּאַ֥ת קָדִ֛מָה עַד־פְּאַת־יָ֖מָּה אֶפְרַ֥יִם אֶחָֽד׃
Next to the territory of Ephraim, from the east side to the west side, Reuben will have one portion.
וְעַ֣ל ׀ גְּב֣וּל אֶפְרַ֗יִם מִפְּאַ֥ת קָדִ֛ים וְעַד־פְּאַת־יָ֖מָּה רְאוּבֵ֥ן אֶחָֽד׃
Next to the territory of Reuben, from the east side to the west side, Judah will have one portion.
וְעַ֣ל ׀ גְּב֣וּל רְאוּבֵ֗ן מִפְּאַ֥ת קָדִ֛ים עַד־פְּאַת־יָ֖מָּה יְהוּדָ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃

Next to the territory of Judah, from the east side to the west side, will be the contribution[^2] you are to set apart, 25,000 wide,[^3] and as long as one of the tribal portions, from the east side to the west side, with the sanctuary in the middle of it.

וְעַל֙ גְּב֣וּל יְהוּדָ֔ה מִפְּאַ֥ת קָדִ֖ים עַד־פְּאַת־יָ֑מָּה תִּהְיֶ֣ה הַתְּרוּמָ֣ה אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־תָּרִ֡ימוּ חֲמִשָּׁה֩ וְעֶשְׂרִ֨ים אֶ֜לֶף רֹ֗חַב וְאֹ֜רֶךְ כְּאַחַ֤ד הַחֲלָקִים֙ מִפְּאַ֤ת קָדִ֙ימָה֙ עַד־פְּאַת־יָ֔מָּה וְהָיָ֥ה הַמִּקְדָּ֖שׁ בְּתוֹכֽוֹ׃
The contribution you are to set apart for the LORD[^4] will be 25,000 long and 10,000 wide.[^5]
הַתְּרוּמָ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּרִ֖ימוּ לַֽיהוָ֑ה אֹ֗רֶךְ חֲמִשָּׁ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף וְרֹ֖חַב עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִֽים׃

This will be the holy contribution for the priests: on the north side 25,000 long, on the west side 10,000 wide, on the east side 10,000 wide, and on the south side 25,000 long. The sanctuary of the LORD will be in the middle of it.

וּ֠לְאֵ֜לֶּה תִּהְיֶ֣ה תְרֽוּמַת־הַקֹּדֶשׁ֮ לַכֹּֽהֲנִים֒ צָפ֜וֹנָה חֲמִשָּׁ֧ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֣ים אֶ֗לֶף וְיָ֙מָּה֙ רֹ֚חַב עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת אֲלָפִ֔ים וְקָדִ֗ימָה רֹ֚חַב עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת אֲלָפִ֔ים וְנֶ֕גְבָּה אֹ֕רֶךְ חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים אָ֑לֶף וְהָיָ֥ה מִקְדַּשׁ־יְהוָ֖ה בְּתוֹכֽוֹ׃
It will be for the consecrated priests, the sons of Zadok,[^6] who kept my charge and did not go astray when the Israelites went astray, as the Levites did.
לַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים הַֽמְקֻדָּשׁ֙ מִבְּנֵ֣י צָד֔וֹק אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמְר֖וּ מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֑י אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־תָע֗וּ בִּתְעוֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּע֖וּ הַלְוִיִּֽם׃ ס
It will be a special portion for them from the holy contribution of the land, a most holy place, next to the territory of the Levites.
וְהָיְתָ֨ה לָהֶ֧ם תְּרוּמִיָּ֛ה מִתְּרוּמַ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ קֹ֣דֶשׁ קָדָשִׁ֑ים אֶל־גְּב֖וּל הַלְוִיִּֽם׃
Alongside the territory of the priests, the Levites will have an area 25,000 long and 10,000 wide. The whole length will be 25,000 and the width 10,000.
וְהַלְוִיִּ֗ם לְעֻמַּת֙ גְּב֣וּל הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים חֲמִשָּׁ֨ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֙לֶף֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ וְרֹ֖חַב עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת אֲלָפִ֑ים כָּל־אֹ֗רֶךְ חֲמִשָּׁ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף וְרֹ֖חַב עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִֽים׃
They must not sell any of it or exchange it, and this choicest part of the land must not pass to others, for it is holy to the LORD.
וְלֹא־יִמְכְּר֣וּ מִמֶּ֗נּוּ וְלֹ֥א יָמֵ֛ר וְלֹ֥א *יעבור **יַעֲבִ֖יר רֵאשִׁ֣ית הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּי־קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַיהוָֽה׃
The remaining area, 5,000 wide and 25,000 long, will be for the common use of the city, for houses and for open land. The city will be in the middle of it.
וַחֲמֵ֨שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֜ים הַנּוֹתָ֣ר בָּרֹ֗חַב עַל־פְּנֵי֙[t] חֲמִשָּׁ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף חֹֽל־ה֣וּא לָעִ֔יר לְמוֹשָׁ֖ב וּלְמִגְרָ֑שׁ וְהָיְתָ֥ה הָעִ֖יר *בתוכה **בְּתוֹכֽוֹ׃
These will be its measurements: the north side 4,500, the south side 4,500,[^7] the east side 4,500 and the west side 4,500.

וְאֵלֶּה֮ מִדּוֹתֶיהָ֒ פְּאַ֣ת צָפ֗וֹן חֲמֵ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ וְאַרְבַּ֣עַת אֲלָפִ֔ים וּפְאַת־נֶ֕גֶב חֲמֵ֥שׁ *חמש מֵא֖וֹת וְאַרְבַּ֣עַת אֲלָפִ֑ים וּמִפְּאַ֣ת קָדִ֗ים חֲמֵ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ וְאַרְבַּ֣עַת אֲלָפִ֔ים וּפְאַת־יָ֕מָּה חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת וְאַרְבַּ֥עַת אֲלָפִֽים׃
The city will have open land: 250 on the north, 250 on the south, 250 on the east and 250 on the west.
וְהָיָ֣ה מִגְרָשׁ֮ לָעִיר֒ צָפ֙וֹנָה֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וּמָאתַ֔יִם וְנֶ֖גְבָּה חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וּמָאתָ֑יִם וְקָדִ֙ימָה֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וּמָאתַ֔יִם וְיָ֖מָּה חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּמָאתָֽיִם׃

The rest of the area, along the length beside the holy contribution, will be 10,000 on the east and 10,000 on the west. It will lie beside the holy contribution, and its produce will be food for the workers of the city.

וְהַנּוֹתָ֨ר בָּאֹ֜רֶךְ לְעֻמַּ֣ת ׀ תְּרוּמַ֣ת הַקֹּ֗דֶשׁ עֲשֶׂ֨רֶת אֲלָפִ֤ים קָדִ֙ימָה֙ וַעֲשֶׂ֤רֶת אֲלָפִים֙ יָ֔מָּה וְהָיָ֕ה לְעֻמַּ֖ת תְּרוּמַ֣ת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ וְהָיְתָ֤ה *תבואתה **תְבֽוּאָתוֹ֙ לְלֶ֔חֶם לְעֹבְדֵ֖י הָעִֽיר׃
The workers of the city, from all the tribes of Israel, will farm it.
וְהָעֹבֵ֖ד הָעִ֑יר יַעַבְד֕וּהוּ מִכֹּ֖ל שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
The whole contribution will be 25,000 by 25,000. You are to set apart the holy contribution as a square, together with the city's property.
כָּל־הַתְּרוּמָ֗ה חֲמִשָּׁ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים אָ֑לֶף רְבִיעִ֗ית תָּרִ֙ימוּ֙ אֶת־תְּרוּמַ֣ת הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ אֶל־אֲחֻזַּ֖ת הָעִֽיר׃

What remains on both sides of the holy contribution and of the city's property will belong to the prince.[^8] It will extend eastward from the 25,000 of the contribution to the eastern border, and westward from the 25,000 to the western border, alongside the tribal portions. It will belong to the prince. The holy contribution and the sanctuary of the house[^9] will be in the middle of it.

וְהַנּוֹתָ֣ר לַנָּשִׂ֣יא מִזֶּ֣ה ׀ וּמִזֶּ֣ה ׀ לִתְרֽוּמַת־הַקֹּ֣דֶשׁ וְלַאֲחֻזַּ֪ת הָעִ֟יר אֶל־פְּנֵ֣י חֲמִשָּׁה֩ וְעֶשְׂרִ֨ים אֶ֥לֶף ׀ תְּרוּמָה֮ עַד־גְּב֣וּל קָדִימָה֒ וְיָ֗מָּה עַל־פְּ֠נֵי חֲמִשָּׁ֨ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֙לֶף֙ עַל־גְּב֣וּל יָ֔מָּה לְעֻמַּ֥ת חֲלָקִ֖ים לַנָּשִׂ֑יא וְהָֽיְתָה֙ תְּרוּמַ֣ת הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ וּמִקְדַּ֥שׁ הַבַּ֖יִת *בתוכה **בְּתוֹכֽוֹ׃

The property of the Levites and the property of the city will lie in the middle of what belongs to the prince; the land between the territory of Judah and the territory of Benjamin will belong to the prince.[^10]
וּמֵאֲחֻזַּ֤ת הַלְוִיִּם֙ וּמֵאֲחֻזַּ֣ת הָעִ֔יר בְּת֛וֹךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לַנָּשִׂ֖יא יִֽהְיֶ֑ה בֵּ֣ין ׀ גְּב֣וּל יְהוּדָ֗ה וּבֵין֙ גְּב֣וּל בִּנְיָמִ֔ן לַנָּשִׂ֖יא יִהְיֶֽה׃
As for the rest of the tribes: from the east side to the west side, Benjamin will have one portion.
וְיֶ֖תֶר הַשְּׁבָטִ֑ים מִפְּאַ֥ת קָדִ֛ימָה עַד־פְּאַת־יָ֖מָּה בִּנְיָמִ֥ן אֶחָֽד׃
Next to the territory of Benjamin, from the east side to the west side, Simeon will have one portion.
וְעַ֣ל ׀ גְּב֣וּל בִּנְיָמִ֗ן מִפְּאַ֥ת קָדִ֛ימָה עַד־פְּאַת־יָ֖מָּה שִׁמְע֥וֹן אֶחָֽד׃
Next to the territory of Simeon, from the east side to the west side, Issachar will have one portion.
וְעַ֣ל ׀ גְּב֣וּל שִׁמְע֗וֹן מִפְּאַ֥ת קָדִ֛ימָה עַד־פְּאַת־יָ֖מָּה יִשָׂשכָ֥ר אֶחָֽד׃
Next to the territory of Issachar, from the east side to the west side, Zebulun will have one portion.
וְעַ֣ל ׀ גְּב֣וּל יִשָׂשכָ֗ר מִפְּאַ֥ת קָדִ֛ימָה עַד־פְּאַת־יָ֖מָּה זְבוּלֻ֥ן אֶחָֽד׃
Next to the territory of Zebulun, from the east side to the west side, Gad will have one portion.
וְעַ֣ל ׀ גְּב֣וּל זְבוּלֻ֗ן מִפְּאַ֥ת קָדִ֛מָה עַד־פְּאַת־יָ֖מָּה גָּ֥ד אֶחָֽד׃
Next to the territory of Gad, on the south side, toward the Negev, the boundary will run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, and along the Wadi to the Great Sea.[^11]
וְעַל֙ גְּב֣וּל גָּ֔ד אֶל־פְּאַ֖ת נֶ֣גֶב תֵּימָ֑נָה וְהָיָ֨ה גְב֜וּל מִתָּמָ֗ר מֵ֚י מְרִיבַ֣ת קָדֵ֔שׁ נַחֲלָ֖ה עַל־הַיָּ֥ם הַגָּדֽוֹל׃
This is the land you are to allot as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel, and these will be their portions, declares the Lord GOD.[^12]
זֹ֥את הָאָ֛רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־תַּפִּ֥ילוּ מִֽנַּחֲלָ֖ה לְשִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ מַחְלְקוֹתָ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ פ
These are the exits of the city: On the north side, which measures 4,500,
וְאֵ֖לֶּה תּוֹצְאֹ֣ת הָעִ֑יר מִפְּאַ֣ת צָפ֔וֹן חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֛וֹת וְאַרְבַּ֥עַת אֲלָפִ֖ים מִדָּֽה׃
the gates of the city will be named after the tribes of Israel. There will be three gates on the north: one gate for Reuben, one gate for Judah and one gate for Levi.
וְשַׁעֲרֵ֣י הָעִ֗יר עַל־שְׁמוֹת֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שְׁעָרִ֥ים שְׁלוֹשָׁ֖ה צָפ֑וֹנָה שַׁ֣עַר רְאוּבֵ֞ן אֶחָ֗ד שַׁ֤עַר יְהוּדָה֙ אֶחָ֔ד שַׁ֥עַר לֵוִ֖י אֶחָֽד׃
On the east side, which measures 4,500, there will be three gates: one gate for Joseph, one gate for Benjamin and one gate for Dan.
וְאֶל־פְּאַ֣ת קָדִ֗ימָה חֲמֵ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ וְאַרְבַּ֣עַת אֲלָפִ֔ים וּשְׁעָרִ֖ים שְׁלֹשָׁ֑ה וְשַׁ֨עַר יוֹסֵ֜ף אֶחָ֗ד שַׁ֤עַר בִּנְיָמִן֙ אֶחָ֔ד שַׁ֥עַר דָּ֖ן אֶחָֽד׃
On the south side, which measures 4,500, there will be three gates: one gate for Simeon, one gate for Issachar and one gate for Zebulun.
וּפְאַת־נֶ֗גְבָּה חֲמֵ֨שׁ מֵא֜וֹת וְאַרְבַּ֤עַת אֲלָפִים֙ מִדָּ֔ה וּשְׁעָרִ֖ים שְׁלֹשָׁ֑ה שַׁ֣עַר שִׁמְע֞וֹן אֶחָ֗ד שַׁ֤עַר יִשָּׂשכָר֙ אֶחָ֔ד שַׁ֥עַר זְבוּלֻ֖ן אֶחָֽד׃
On the west side, which measures 4,500, there will be three gates: one gate for Gad, one gate for Asher and one gate for Naphtali.
פְּאַת־יָ֗מָּה חֲמֵ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ וְאַרְבַּ֣עַת אֲלָפִ֔ים שַֽׁעֲרֵיהֶ֖ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֑ה שַׁ֣עַר גָּ֞ד אֶחָ֗ד שַׁ֤עַר אָשֵׁר֙ אֶחָ֔ד שַׁ֥עַר נַפְתָּלִ֖י אֶחָֽד׃
The distance all around will be 18,000.[^13] And from that day on the name of the city will be 'The LORD Is There.'"[^14]
סָבִ֕יב שְׁמֹנָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אָ֑לֶף וְשֵׁם־הָעִ֥יר מִיּ֖וֹם יְהוָ֥ה ׀ שָֽׁמָּה׃

n.1: Literally "and they will be his, the east side, the sea". Each tribe's portion is a strip running across the land from east to west, from the Jordan to the Mediterranean (47:15–20). Compare Joshua 13–19, where the tribes receive very different territories.
n.2: Hebrew *terumah*: something set apart and given for a sacred purpose (45:1). Also in verses 9–10, 12, 18 and 20–21.
n.3: The unit is not given; probably the long cubit of 40:5 (about 21 inches or 53 cm), as in 45:1, so that 25,000 was about 8 miles (13 km). The same is true of the other measurements in this chapter.
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: This is perhaps the priests' portion (verses 10–12), which lies beside the Levites' portion of the same size (verse 13). Compare 45:1–5.
n.7: The Hebrew text writes the word "five" twice here, but it is read only once.
n.8: Hebrew *nasi*, "leader, chief", the ruler of Israel (44:3; 45:7–8).
n.9: That is, the temple, as throughout chapters 40–48.
n.10: Literally "And from the property of the Levites and from the property of the city, in the middle of what is for the prince it will be; between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin, it will be for the prince." The meaning is uncertain.
n.12: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles.
n.13: About 6 miles (9.5 km), if the unit is the long cubit.
n.14: Hebrew *YHWH shammah*.
